akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يُظَاهِرُونَ﴾, light and heavy. Whoever reads it heavy makes it from "تَظَهَّرْت" and then assimilates the tāʾ into the ẓāʾ.

akhfash:3-3.t: And His word ﴿ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُواْ فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ﴾: the meaning is: "then (the duty is) the freeing of a slave before they touch each other; and whoever does not find (the means), the feeding of sixty poor persons; then they return to what they said: 'that we will not do it', and they do it". This is the ẓihār: he says "she is to me like my mother's back" and similar speech. When he has freed a slave or fed sixty poor persons, he returns to that of which he said "it is forbidden to me" and does it.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ have you not looked ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا﴾: they are the hypocrites; ﴿قَوْمًا﴾: they are the Jews; ﴿غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مَا هُمْ﴾, i.e. the hypocrites, ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ of the believers ﴿وَلَا مِنْهُمْ﴾ of the Jews; rather, they waver in between. ﴿وَيَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ﴾, i.e. their statement that they are believers, ﴿وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that they are lying in it.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا إِنَّهُمْ سَاءَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of acts of disobedience.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً﴾ a cover over their persons and their property, ﴿فَصَدُّوا﴾ the believers by means of them ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾, i.e. from fighting against them by killing them and taking their property; ﴿فَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ possessing humiliation.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ from His punishment ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ of availing; ﴿أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾. Mention:

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ﴾ that they are believers, ﴿كَمَا يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلَى شَيْءٍ﴾ of benefit from their oath in the Hereafter, as in this world. ﴿أَلَا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْكَاذِبُونَ﴾

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿اسْتَحْوَذَ﴾ has gained mastery ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ through their obeying him, ﴿فَأَنْسَاهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ his followers. ﴿أَلَا إِنَّ حِزْبَ الشَّيْطَانِ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ﴾ who oppose ﴿اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ أُولَئِكَ فِي الْأَذَلِّينَ﴾ the overcome.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿كَتَبَ اللَّهُ﴾ in the Preserved Tablet, or: He decreed, ﴿لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي﴾ by proof or by the sword. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿لَا تَجِدُ قَوْمًا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ يُوَادُّونَ﴾ befriending ﴿مَنْ حَادَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَوْ كَانُوا﴾, i.e. those who oppose, ﴿آبَاءَهُمْ﴾, i.e. of the believers, ﴿أَوْ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوَانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ﴾; rather, they set out against them with harm and fight them over faith, as happened with a group of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ who do not befriend them, ﴿كَتَبَ﴾ He has established ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَأَيَّدَهُمْ بِرُوحٍ﴾ with a light ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ the Exalted, ﴿وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ﴾ for their obedience to Him ﴿وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ with His reward. ﴿أُولَئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ﴾: they follow His command and avoid what He forbids. ﴿أَلَا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ the winners.

celaleyn:1-1.t:
﴿قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجَادِلُكَ﴾ who argues with you, O Prophet, ﴿فِي زَوْجِهَا﴾ who had pronounced ẓihār on her. He had said to her: "You are to me like my mother's back." She asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, and he answered her that she had become unlawful to him, according to what was customary among them, namely that ẓihār entails permanent separation. She is Khawla bint Thaʿlaba, and he is Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit. ﴿وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ her loneliness, her poverty, and young children who, if I placed them with him, would be lost, or with her, would go hungry; ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَا﴾ your exchange of words; ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾ knowing.
[Translator's note: the source shifts from "her" to "I" within the quoted complaint ("if I placed them with him … or with her"); translated as written.]

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَظَّهَّرُونَ﴾ its original form is يَتَظَهَّرُونَ, and the tāʾ was assimilated into the ẓāʾ; and in one reading with an alif between the ẓāʾ and the light hāʾ, and in another [يُظَاهِرُونَ], like يُقَاتِلُونَ; and the second place is likewise; ﴿مِنْكُمْ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ مَا هُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ إِنْ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّائِي﴾ with hamza and yāʾ, and without yāʾ, ﴿وَلَدْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمْ﴾ by ẓihār ﴿لَيَقُولُونَ مُنْكَرًا مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَزُورًا﴾ a lie; ﴿وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾ to the one who pronounces ẓihār, through the expiation (kaffāra).

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَظَّهَّرُونَ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُوا﴾ in it, by going against it through keeping the wife on whom ẓihār was pronounced, which is contrary to the intent of ẓihār, namely describing the woman as unlawful, ﴿فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ﴾ that is, freeing one is incumbent on him, ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا﴾ by intercourse; ﴿ذَلِكُمْ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ﴾ a slave, ﴿فَصِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا فَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ﴾ that is, the fasting, ﴿فَإِطْعَامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا﴾ is incumbent on him, that is, before they touch each other, by applying the unrestricted (muṭlaq) to the restricted (muqayyad); for each poor person a mudd of the staple food of the land. ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ that is, the lightening of the expiation, ﴿لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَتِلْكَ﴾ that is, the rulings mentioned, ﴿حُدُودُ اللَّهِ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in them ﴿عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ﴾ oppose ﴿اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ كُبِتُوا﴾ were humiliated ﴿كَمَا كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ in their opposing their messengers; ﴿وَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ﴾ pointing to the truthfulness of the Messenger; ﴿وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in the signs ﴿عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ bringing humiliation,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾. [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ do you not know ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مَا يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ﴾ by His knowledge, ﴿وَلَا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ وَلَا أَدْنَى مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كَانُوا ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ look ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ نُهُوا عَنِ النَّجْوَى ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ وَيَتَنَاجَوْنَ بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَمَعْصِيَتِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ they are the Jews; the Prophet ﷺ forbade them what they used to do of their secret conversation, that is, talking secretly while looking at the believers, to put suspicion into their hearts; ﴿وَإِذَا جَاءُوكَ حَيَّوْكَ﴾ O Prophet ﴿بِمَا لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ﴾ and it is their saying "al-sām ʿalayka", that is, death; ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَوْلَا﴾ why does not ﴿يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ بِمَا نَقُولُ﴾ of the greeting, and that he is not a prophet, if he is a prophet? ﴿حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ is it.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا تَنَاجَيْتُمْ فَلَا تَتَنَاجَوْا بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَمَعْصِيَتِ الرَّسُولِ وَتَنَاجَوْا بِالْبِرِّ وَالتَّقْوَى وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا النَّجْوَى﴾ in sin and the like ﴿مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ through his deception, ﴿لِيَحْزُنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَيْسَ﴾ he ﴿بِضَارِّهِمْ شَيْئًا إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, His will; ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا قِيلَ لَكُمْ تَفَسَّحُوا﴾ make room ﴿فِي الْمَجْلِسِ﴾ the gathering of the Prophet ﷺ and of remembrance, so that whoever comes to you may sit — and in one reading [الْمَجَالِسِ] — ﴿فَافْسَحُوا يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ﴾ in Paradise; ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ انْشِزُوا﴾ rise for prayer and other good deeds, ﴿فَانْشِزُوا﴾ — and in one reading with ḍamma on the shīn in both [انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا] — ﴿يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ﴾ through obedience in that, ﴿وَ﴾ He raises ﴿الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجَاتٍ﴾ in Paradise; ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا نَاجَيْتُمُ الرَّسُولَ﴾ you wish to converse with him privately, ﴿فَقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْوَاكُمْ﴾ before it ﴿صَدَقَةً ذَلِكَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَأَطْهَرُ﴾ for your sins; ﴿فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدُوا﴾ anything to give in charity, ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ for your private conversation, ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to you — meaning: there is no blame on you in private conversation without charity. Then that was abrogated by His words:

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿أَأَشْفَقْتُمْ﴾ with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed into an alif, and softened, and with an alif inserted between the softened one and the other, and without it; that is, did you fear ﴿أَنْ تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْوَاكُمْ صَدَقَاتٍ﴾ because of poverty? ﴿فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا﴾ the charity ﴿وَتَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ turned you back from it, ﴿فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَوةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَوةَ وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ that is, persevere in that; ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

daas-irab:1-1.t:
﴿قَدْ سَمِعَ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq) and a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿قَوْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is muḍāf. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿تُجادِلُكَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي زَوْجِها﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَتَشْتَكِي﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَسْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿تَحاوُرَكُما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ﴾ inna, its noun (ism) and its two khabars; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾ negative, operating like ليس. ﴿هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾ its noun (ism) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of الذين, and the clause الذين.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative. ﴿أُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿اللَّائِي﴾ the relative noun is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلَدْنَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿لَيَقُولُونَ﴾ the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of إنهم, and the nominal clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿مُنْكَراً﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ a ṣifa of منكر. ﴿وَزُوراً﴾ conjoined to منكرا. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾ inna and its noun, the shifted lām, and عفو غفور are two khabars; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُظاهِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَعُودُونَ﴾ conjoined to يظاهرون. ﴿لِما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿فَتَحْرِيرُ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and تحرير is a mubtadaʾ, and it is muḍāf. ﴿رَقَبَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; the nominal clause is the khabar of الذين, and the clause الذين.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ both attached to تحرير. ﴿أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the alif is its fāʿil; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ذلِكُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿تُوعَظُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to خبير. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَمْ يَجِدْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿فَصِيامُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and صيام is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is omitted. ﴿شَهْرَيْنِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُتَتابِعَيْنِ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of شهرين; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clauses of the condition and its apodosis are the khabar of من. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) صيام. ﴿أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the alif is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; a conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by لم. ﴿فَإِطْعامُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective. ﴿إطعام﴾ a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, and the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من.., and the clause فمن لم.. is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿سِتِّينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ. ﴿مِسْكِيناً﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِتُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an أن concealed after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ a ṣifa of عذاب; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿يُحَادُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كُبِتُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كَما كُبِتَ﴾ the kāf is a preposition of comparison (tashbīh), ما is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and a passive past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila of the relative noun; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from ما and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿أَنْزَلْنا آياتٍ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿بَيِّناتٍ﴾ a ṣifa of آيات; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُهِينٌ﴾ a ṣifa of عذاب; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَحْصاهُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَنَسُوهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both attached to شهيد. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿شَهِيدٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir). ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna and its noun (ism). ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause ألم تر.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿يَكُونُ﴾ a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ نَجْوى﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) من, nominative in position as the fāʿil of يكون. ﴿ثَلاثَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). The wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿خَمْسَةٍ﴾ conjoined to ثلاثة. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿هُوَ سادِسُهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿أَدْنى﴾ conjoined to the form (lafẓ) of نجوى. ﴿مِنْ ذلِكَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) أدنى. ﴿وَلا أَكْثَرَ﴾ conjoined to ولا أدنى. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction. ﴿هُوَ مَعَهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿أَيْنَ ما﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place, and ما is redundant. ﴿كانُوا﴾ a complete past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يُنَبِّئُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿عَمِلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿أَنَّ﴾ but parses it as إنّ; the Quranic text has ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾.] ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ both attached to عليم. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ the khabar of إن; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ see the previous verse. ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿نُهُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَنِ النَّجْوى﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿يَعُودُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لِما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿نُهُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَتَناجَوْنَ﴾ conjoined to يعودون. ﴿بِالْإِثْمِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَالْعُدْوانِ﴾ conjoined to الإثم. ﴿وَمَعْصِيَةِ﴾ conjoined to العدوان. ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِذا﴾ an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿جاؤُكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿حَيَّوْكَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿لَوْلا﴾ a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿يُعَذِّبُنَا﴾ an imperfect verb and its object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil. ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause يعذبنا is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿نَقُولُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يَصْلَوْنَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its object; the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَبِئْسَ﴾ an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm). ﴿الْمَصِيرُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial (ẓarfiyya), non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَناجَيْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَلا تَتَناجَوْا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿بِالْإِثْمِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَالْعُدْوانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ﴾ both conjoined to الإثم. ﴿الرَّسُولِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَتَناجَوْا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِالْبِرِّ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَالتَّقْوى﴾ conjoined to البر. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of الله. ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to تحشرون. ﴿تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ the restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿النَّجْوى﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position.
﴿لِيَحْزُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَيْسَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun (ism) latent (mustatir). ﴿بِضارِّهِمْ﴾ genitive in form, accusative in position as the khabar of ليس. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿بِإِذْنِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ a conjunction, and both attached to يتوكل. ﴿فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command (lām al-amr). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا﴾ its i'rab has gone before. ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿تَفَسَّحُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي الْمَجالِسِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿فَافْسَحُوا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿يَفْسَحِ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَإِذا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا﴾ the i'rab of its like has gone before. ﴿يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ the relative noun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿الْعِلْمَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿دَرَجاتٍ﴾ accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾ its i'rab has preceded.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿ناجَيْتُمُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿الرَّسُولَ﴾ its object; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فَقَدِّمُوا﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place, and it is muḍāf. ﴿يَدَيْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿نَجْواكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿صَدَقَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿ذلِكَ خَيْرٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير. ﴿وَأَطْهَرُ﴾ conjoined to خير. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and إن is conditional. ﴿لَمْ تَجِدُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun (ism) and its two khabars; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:13-13.t:
﴿أَأَشْفَقْتُمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَنْ تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition, and the clause أشفقتم is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْواكُمْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿صَدَقاتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا﴾ إذ is an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw is its fāʿil; and the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa), and the clause إذ is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَتابَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the response (jawāb) of إذ, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ، وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ both conjoined to what precedes them.
﴿وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ its i'rab has preceded.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ألم تر is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿غَضِبَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of قوما. ﴿ما﴾ negative, without operation. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ conjoined to منكم. ﴿وَيَحْلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلَى الْكَذِبِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ, and يعلمون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of هم, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿شَدِيداً﴾ a ṣifa (adjective). ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿ساءَ﴾ a past verb for expressing blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm), and the fāʿil is necessarily latent (mustatir). ﴿ما﴾ an indefinite noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of the accusative as tamyīz (specification); the clause ساء is the khabar (predicate) of إن, and the clause إنهم.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿كانُوا﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كانوا, and the verbal clause is a ṣifa of ما.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَيْمانَهُمْ﴾ its first object. ﴿جُنَّةً﴾ its second object; the verbal clause is explicative (mufassira) of the clause ساء... ﴿فَصَدُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَلَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُهِينٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of عذاب; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿لَنْ تُغْنِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَمْوالُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ﴾ conjoined to أموالهم. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to تغني. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿النَّارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to خالدون. ﴿خالِدُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time, and an imperfect verb and its object. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَيَحْلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to يبعثهم. ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَما﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿يَحْلِفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, the wāw its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَيَحْسَبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun (ism). ﴿عَلى شَيْءٍ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of أنهم; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسبون. ﴿أَلا﴾ a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh) and opening (istiftāḥ). ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ but parses it as إنّ; the Quranic text has ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾.] ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْكاذِبُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿اسْتَحْوَذَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَأَنْساهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿ذِكْرَ﴾ its second object. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَلا﴾ a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh) and opening (istiftāḥ). ﴿إِنَّ حِزْبَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: in both places the source prints the muḍāf ilayhi as ﴿الشَّيْطانُ﴾ with ḍamma; the Quranic text has ﴿الشَّيْطانِ﴾.] ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْخاسِرُونَ﴾ the khabar of إن; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي الْأَذَلِّينَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause أولئك is the khabar of إن, and the clause إن is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿كَتَبَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَأَغْلِبَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis. ﴿أَنَا﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) fāʿil. ﴿وَرُسُلِي﴾ conjoined to أنا; the clause is the response to the omitted oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾ inna, its noun (ism) and its two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:22-22.t:
﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَجِدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of قوما. ﴿وَالْيَوْمِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿الْآخِرِ﴾ a ṣifa of اليوم; the clause لا تجد..
is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُوادُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿حَادَّ اللَّهَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent, and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to الله; and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is for the ḥāl, and لو is connective (waṣliyya). ﴿كانُوا آباءَهُمْ﴾ kāna, its noun (ism) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to آباءهم. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿كَتَبَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of أولئك, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْإِيمانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَيَّدَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent. ﴿بِرُوحٍ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a ṣifa of روح; the clause is conjoined to كتب. ﴿وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿تَجْرِي﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿مِنْ تَحْتِهَا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الْأَنْهارُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is a ṣifa of جنات. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl. ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to خالدين. ﴿رَضِيَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ with fatḥa; as muḍāf ilayhi the Quranic text has ﴿اللَّهِ﴾.] The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ its i'rab has preceded at no. 19.

dervis-irab:14-17.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا قَوْماً غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ): a resumptive statement brought to express wonder at the state of the hypocrites, who used to take the Jews as allies, giving them counsel and divulging the secrets of the believers to them. Al-Suddī said: "It has reached us that it was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nufayl, one of the hypocrites." The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī); لم is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and jussive; تر is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; إلى الذين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تر; the clause تولوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position, and the wāw is the fāʿil; قوما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause غضب الله عليهم is a naʿt (adjective) of قوما.
(ما هُمْ مِنْكُمْ وَلا مِنْهُمْ): the clause is resumptive, or a second adjective of قوما, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of تولوا. ما is the Ḥijāzī negating ما, هم is its noun and منكم its predicate; ولا: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negating; منهم is conjoined to منكم.
(وَيَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; يحلفون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the clause is conjoined to تولوا, so it falls within the scope of the ṣila; على الكذب is a ḥāl; the wāw is circumstantial; هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يعلمون is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl.
(أَعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهُمْ عَذاباً شَدِيداً إِنَّهُمْ ساءَ ما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ): a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; and إنّ with its noun and its predicate.
(اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ جُنَّةً فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): the clause is resumptive, or a third adjective of قوما, or a ḥāl. اتخذوا is a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; أيمانهم is the first mafʿūl bihi and جنة the second mafʿūl bihi of اتخذوا, i.e. a cover and protection for themselves and their property. فصدّوا: the fāʿ is conjunctive and صدّوا is a past verb with its fāʿil; عن سبيل الله is attached to صدّوا.
(فَلَهُمْ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): the fāʿ is conjunctive; لهم is a fronted khabar, عذاب a postponed mubtadaʾ, and مهين an adjective of عذاب, i.e. possessing humiliation.
(لَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ أَمْوالُهُمْ وَلا أَوْلادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ شَيْئاً): لن is a particle of negation, accusative and futurity; تغني is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by لن; عنهم is attached to تغني; أموالهم is the fāʿil; ولا أولادهم is conjoined to أموالهم; من الله is attached to تغني with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "from the punishment of Allah"; and شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. even a little of availing.
(أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and أصحاب النار its khabar; هم is a mubtadaʾ, فيها is attached to خالدون, and خالدون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The scholars of rhetoric have mentioned four views on the definition of truth and falsehood:
1- That truth is the conformity of the statement's judgement to reality, and falsehood its non-conformity to it, even if the belief [of the speaker] is otherwise in both cases.
2- This is the view of al-Naẓẓām, one of the great Muʿtazilites: that truth is conformity to the belief of the informant, even if mistaken, and falsehood is non-conformity to the belief, even if correct. [A statement made] with no belief accompanying it falls, on this view, within falsehood; there is no intermediate category.
3- This is the view of al-Jāḥiẓ, also one of the masters of the Muʿtazila: that truth is conformity to external reality together with the informant's belief in that conformity, and falsehood is non-conformity to reality together with the belief in its non-conformity; anything other than that is neither truth nor falsehood, i.e. an intermediate between them. This comprises four cases: the conforming with no belief in anything; the conforming with a belief in non-conformity; the non-conforming with a belief in conformity; and the non-conforming with no belief.
4- This is the view of al-Rāghib; it is like the view of al-Jāḥiẓ, except that he described the four cases as true and false under two considerations: truth in respect of conformity to external reality or to belief, and falsehood in respect of the absence of conformity to external reality or to belief.
Al-Naẓẓām adduced as proof the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إن المنافقين لكاذبون», i.e. in their saying «إنك لرسول الله», because it did not conform to their belief. His argument was refuted on the grounds that what is meant is that they are liars in the testimony, i.e. in their claim that the heart agrees with the tongue, since their saying "إنك ..." etc. implies "our testimony is from the depths of the heart", and this is a lie.
Al-Jāḥiẓ adduced as proof the saying of Allah the Exalted: «افترى على الله كذبا أم به جنة», because informing while in a state of madness is other than lying, since it is set against it as a separate category, and other than truth, since they believed he was not truthful; thus the intermediate category is established. This was refuted on the grounds that the meaning is "or has he not fabricated", and the absence of fabrication was expressed by madness inasmuch as a madman has no fabrication, because fabrication is deliberate lying. So this is a restriction of the false statement, by their claim, into its two kinds, i.e. lying deliberately and not deliberately.
* Vocabulary:
(اسْتَحْوَذَ): he took control and prevailed; from حاذ الحمار العانة, i.e. the wild ass gathered the herd and drove it, prevailing over it; and from it: "he was an أحوذي, unique of his kind". It is one of the words that came according to the original form, like استصوب and استنوق, i.e. contrary to the analogical rule, for the analogical form would be استحاذ, with the wāw turned into alif, as in استعاذ and استقام; but استحوذ here is better.
(يُحَادُّونَ): they oppose.

dervis-irab:18-22.t:
* I'rab:
(يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ): يوم is accusative (manṣūb) by an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember), and the clause is resumptive; the clause يبعثهم is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being annexed to it; الله is the fāʿil (agent) of يبعثهم; جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the fāʿ is conjunctive; يحلفون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; له is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يحلفون; كما is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); the clause يحلفون has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative [ما]; and لكم is attached to يحلفون.
(وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ): the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause يحسبون is a ḥāl from the wāw in يحلفون له, i.e. while they think in the Hereafter that their swearing there will benefit them against its punishment. أنّ and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) filling the place of the two objects of يحسبون; على شيء is the khabar (predicate) of أنهم. ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنّ with its noun; هم is an attached pronoun [Translator's note: so in the source; the parallel passages below say "a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl)", which is presumably what is meant] or a mubtadaʾ (subject); الكاذبون is the khabar of إنهم on the first view, and its [هم's] khabar on the second, the clause then being the khabar of إنهم.
(اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ فَأَنْساهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ): a resumptive statement brought to explain Satan's control over them, to the point that he made them his followers and his flock. عليهم is attached to استحوذ and الشيطان is its fāʿil; فأنساهم is conjoined to استحوذ, the hāʾ being the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and ذكر الله the second mafʿūl bihi.
(أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطانِ أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ الشَّيْطانِ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and حزب الشيطان the khabar; ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنّ with its noun; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; and الخاسرون is the khabar in both cases, as has preceded.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ أُولئِكَ فِي الْأَذَلِّينَ): إنّ and its noun; the clause يحادون is the ṣila; الله is the mafʿūl bihi and رسوله is conjoined to الله; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and في الأذلين is the khabar of أولئك, and the clause is the khabar of إنّ.
(كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ): كتب الله is a verb and its fāʿil; the verb كتب carries the meaning of an oath, and the lām is its answer; أغلبنّ is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis; أنا is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent fāʿil of أغلبنّ; رسلي is conjoined to the pronoun; and إنّ with its noun and its two predicates; and the clauses have no grammatical position.
(لا تَجِدُ قَوْماً يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ يُوادُّونَ مَنْ حَادَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: «This is of the category of imaginative representation (takhyīl): it is represented that it is impossible and absurd that you should find a people who are believers taking the idolaters as allies; and the purpose of this is that this ought not to be, and its due is that it be impossible and not exist in any circumstance, by way of exaggeration in forbidding it and deterring from involvement in it, and enjoining firmness in avoiding the enemies of Allah and keeping far from them, and guarding against mixing and associating with them.» لا is negating; تجد is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنت"; قوما is the first mafʿūl bihi; the clause يؤمنون بالله واليوم الآخر is a naʿt (adjective) of قوما; the clause يوادّون is the second object of تجد if it means "know", and if it means "come upon", the clause is a ḥāl or a second adjective of قوما. يوادّون is a verb and its fāʿil; من is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause حاد الله is the ṣila, with no grammatical position; حاد الله is a past verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; and رسوله is conjoined to الله.
(وَلَوْ كانُوا آباءَهُمْ أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; كان with its noun, and آباءهم is its predicate, what follows being conjoined to it. The secret of the ordering will come in the section on rhetoric.
(أُولئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْإِيمانَ وَأَيَّدَهُمْ بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and the clause كتب is the khabar; في قلوبهم is attached to كتب; الإيمان is the mafʿūl bihi; أيدهم is a verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; بروح is attached to أيدهم; and منه is an adjective of روح.
(وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها): the wāw is conjunctive; يدخلهم is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; جنات is a second mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); the clause تجري من تحتها الأنهار is an adjective of جنات; خالدين is a ḥāl; and فيها is attached to خالدين.
(رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ): رضي is a past verb and الله its fāʿil; عنهم is attached to رضي; ورضوا عنه is conjoined to what precedes. أولئك is a mubtadaʾ and حزب الله the khabar; ألا is a particle of opening and alerting; إنّ with its noun; هم is a pronoun of separation or a mubtadaʾ; and المفلحون is the khabar. The like of this has preceded many times.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «ولو كانوا آباءهم أو أبناءهم أو إخوانهم أو عشيرتهم» a wonderful ordering has been observed. He began first with the fathers, because they most call for concern for them, owing to the obligation of sincere obedience to them; and despite that, He forbade them from loving them. Allah the Exalted said:
«وإن جاهداك لتشرك بي ما ليس لك به علم فلا تطعهما وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا». Secondly He mentioned the sons, because they cling most closely to the core of the heart; then thirdly the brothers, because they are the refuge in time of need and the helper when crises break out, as it has been said:
أخاك أخاك إن من لا أخا له ... كساع إلى الهيجا بغير سلاح
(Your brother, your brother! For whoever has no brother is like one running into battle without a weapon.)
Then fourthly the kinsfolk, because they are the ones whose help is sought in hardships; they are the refuge and the resort in calamities, and they are the ones who hasten to give aid. [The poet] said:
لا يسألون أخاهم حين يندبهم ... في النائبات على ما قال برهانا
(They do not ask their brother, when he calls on them in calamities, for proof of what he says.)
Those intended in the verse are Abū ʿUbayda, because he killed his father on the day of Uḥud; Abū Bakr, because he challenged his son to single combat on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered him to sit back; Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, because he killed his brother Abū ʿAzīz on the day of Uḥud; and ʿAlī and others who killed members of their clans.

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَظْهَرُونَ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse reads «يُظاهِرُونَ»]: the imperfect of «ظاهر». It was also read «يظّهّرون» with doubling of the ẓāʾ and the hāʾ; and «يتظاهرون», the imperfect of «تظاهر», and «يتظهّرون», the imperfect of «تظهّر». What is meant by all of it is ẓihār, which is a man's saying to his wife "You are to me like my mother's back", meaning with respect to prohibition — as though it alluded to riding, since that is known on the backs of animals — and the meaning is that he does not mount her, just as he does not mount his mother. In al-Qāmūs: "Ẓihār is his saying to his wife 'You are to me like my mother's back'; and «ظاهر منها», «تظهّر» and «ظهّر» [are said]." More discussion of this root will come in the Benefits section.

* I'rab:
(قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِها وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ): «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «سمع الله» is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) — al-Kisāʾī assimilated the dāl into the sīn; «قول» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «التي» is a relative noun in the position of genitive by annexation; the clause «تجادلك» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. «تجادلك» is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to the woman mentioned — her story will come in the Benefits section — and the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi. (For this reason the surah was named al-Mujādila, with kasra on the dāl, as an active participle; it was also said with fatḥa and with kasra, as in the gloss of al-Shihāb on al-Bayḍāwī; the kasra is preferable in any case because it is more suited to the context.) «في زوجها» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تجادلك», and a muḍāf must be omitted, i.e. "concerning the affair of her husband". «تشتكي» is conjoined to «تجادلك»; it is also permissible that the wāw be circumstantial and the clause in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «إلى الله» is attached to «تشتكي».
(وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحاوُرَكُما إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause «يسمع» the khabar (predicate); the fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah; «تحاوركما» is the mafʿūl bihi. Ḥiwār in speech is well known. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«حاورته» means I exchanged speech with him; «تحاورا» [they conversed]; and «أحار الرجل الجواب», with alif, means he returned it; and «ما أحاره» means he did not return it." [Then] «إنّ» and its noun and its two predicates, and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya) for what precedes it.
(الَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to begin explaining the rulings on the one who makes ẓihār. «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «يظاهرون» is the ṣila and has no grammatical position; «منكم» is a ḥāl, i.e. in the state of their being from among you, O Arabs; and what is in this ḥāl of disparagement of their customs and rebuke of them is not hidden. «من نسائهم» is attached to «يظاهرون», i.e. they forbid their wives to themselves like Allah's forbidding to them the backs of their mothers. «ما» is the Ḥijāzī negating «ما» [which operates like «ليس»]; «هنّ» is its noun and «أمهاتهم» its khabar, made accusative with the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, which is the relative noun.
(إِنْ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّائِي وَلَدْنَهُمْ): «إن» is negating; «أمهاتهم» is a mubtadaʾ; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «اللائي» is a relative noun in the position of nominative as khabar; the clause «ولدنهم» is the ṣila; «ولدنهم» is a verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi.
(وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنْكَراً مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَزُوراً): the wāw is a conjunction; «إنهم» is «إنّ» and its noun; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «يقولون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of «إنهم»; «منكرا» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a reprehensible saying"; «زورا» is conjoined to «منكرا».
(وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «إنّ» and its noun, and the shifted lām; «عفوّ» is a first khabar and «غفور» a second khabar.
(وَالَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما قالُوا فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا): resumptive speech, set forth to detail the ruling on ẓihār after explaining that it is reprehensible; you may also conjoin the speech to what preceded so that the ruling is arranged in a primary arrangement. «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «يظاهرون» is the ṣila; «من نسائهم» is attached to «يظاهرون». «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «يعودون» is conjoined to «يظاهرون». «لما»: the lām is a preposition and «ما» is maṣdar-forming, and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يعودون», i.e. they return to their saying. You may also make «ما» a relative noun with the clause as its ṣila and the referring pronoun omitted, i.e. "to what they said". The fāʾ links [the predicate] because of the meaning of condition in the relative noun; «تحرير رقبة» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "upon him is the freeing of a slave", and the clause is the khabar of «الذين». «من قبل» is attached to an omitted ḥāl; «أن» with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of genitive by annexation.
(ذلِكُمْ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ): «ذلكم» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the ruling mentioned; the clause «توعظون» is the khabar — for penalties are deterrents from committing crimes. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ; «بما» is attached to «خبير»; the clause «تعملون» is the ṣila; «خبير» is the khabar of «الله».
(فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «من» is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «يجد» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», and the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "هو". «فصيام»: the fāʾ is linking and «صيام» is a mubtadaʾ; «شهرين» is muḍāf ilayhi and «متتابعين» an adjective; the khabar is omitted, i.e. "upon him", and the clause is the khabar of «من». The i'rab of «من قبل أن يتماسا» has preceded.
(فَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَإِطْعامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً): its i'rab has preceded; «مسكينا» is a tamyīz (specification).
(ذلِكَ لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ): «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the foregoing explanation and teaching; «لتؤمنوا»: the lām of causation, and what it enters upon is the khabar of «ذلك». It is also permissible to parse the demonstrative as accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "We did that so that you may believe". «بالله» is attached to «تؤمنوا»; «رسوله» is conjoined to «الله».
(وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «حدود الله» the khabar; the wāw is a conjunction; «للكافرين» is a fronted khabar and «عذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «أليم» is an adjective of «عذاب».

* Rhetoric:
In the verse of ẓihār there is a wonderful device among the devices of rhetoric, namely negation and affirmation (al-salb wa-l-ījāb). Reference to it has preceded: it is building the speech on denying a thing from one aspect and affirming it from another aspect, or commanding a thing from one aspect and forbidding it from a second aspect. In His saying «الذين يظاهرون منكم من نسائهم ما هن أمهاتهم إن أمهاتهم إلا اللائي ولدنهم» there is a denial that the wife becomes a mother through ẓihār, and an affirmation of motherhood for the one who gave birth to the child.

* Benefits:
He said in al-Kashshāf: "ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: 'Praise be to Allah whose hearing encompasses all voices. The woman who disputed spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in a corner of the house while I was with him, and I could not hear, yet He heard her.' And it is reported from ʿUmar that when she came in to him he would honour her and say: 'Allah has heard her.'" As for the woman, she is Khawla bint Thaʿlaba, the wife of Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, her paternal cousin. He saw her praying — she was comely and of beautiful body — and when she finished with the salām he sought intercourse with her, but she refused. He became angry — he had a touch of madness — and said: "You are to me like my mother's back." She came to the Messenger of Allah and complained to him of her affair. It is reported that she said to him: "I have small children; if I leave them with him they will be lost, and if I keep them with me they will go hungry." He said: "I have nothing concerning your affair." It is also reported that he said to her: "I do not see you except that you have become forbidden to him, and I have not been commanded anything regarding you." She said: "I complain to Allah of my poverty and my grief." So these verses were revealed. The rulings on ẓihār and the schools of the imams concerning it are set out at length in the books of jurisprudence, so refer to them if you wish.

dervis-irab:5-7.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُحَادُّونَ): they show enmity and opposition. The wording of al-Zajjāj: muḥādda is that you are on a boundary (ḥadd) different from your companion's boundary; so muḥādda is a metonymy (kināya) for enmity, since it is a necessary concomitant of enmity. In the lexicons: "«حادّه» means he was hostile to him and angered him."
(كُبِتُوا): they were seized and destroyed; it was also said: they were humiliated. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«كبت الله العدو كبتا», of the pattern «ضرب», means He disgraced him and humiliated him; and «كبته لوجهه» means he threw him down on his face."

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ كُبِتُوا كَما كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to convey good tidings to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers of the subduing of their enemies, their humiliation, the breaking of their bonds and the splitting of their unity. «إنّ» and its noun; the clause «يحادون» is the ṣila (relative clause); «الله» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «رسوله» is conjoined to «الله»; the clause «كبتوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ». «كما» is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); the clause «كبت» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative [i.e. the maṣdar-forming «ما»]; «الذين» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «من قبلهم» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element that is the ṣila of «الذين».
(وَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنا آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ): the wāw is circumstantial; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «أنزلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «آيات» is the mafʿūl bihi and «بيّنات» an adjective of «آيات»; «للكافرين» is a fronted khabar and «عذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); «مهين» is an adjective.
(يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا أَحْصاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ): the adverb may be attached to «مهين»; it was also said that its governor is «عذاب»; it was said that its governor is the settling (istiqrār) to which the khabar, namely «للكافرين», is attached; and it was said that it is accusative by an implied "remember". The clause «يبعثهم» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; «الله» is the fāʿil of «يبعثهم»; «جميعا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «فينبئهم» is conjoined to «يبعثهم»; «بما عملوا» is in the position of the second object; the clause «عملوا» is the ṣila of the relative noun. The clause «أحصاه الله» is resumptive; the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause «نسوه» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object of «أحصى», with an implied «قد» or without it.
(وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ): «الله» is a mubtadaʾ; «على كل شيء» is attached to «شهيد»; «شهيد» is the khabar of «الله».
(أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ): the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «تر» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. «أنّ» and its noun, and the clause «يعلم» is its khabar, and it stands in place of the two objects of «تر». «ما» is the object of «يعلم»; «في السموات» is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila of the relative noun; «ما في الأرض» is conjoined to «ما في السموات».
(ما يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوى ثَلاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ وَلا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سادِسُهُمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to affirm the vastness of His knowledge, the Exalted, and to explain its manner. «ما» is negating; «يكون» is a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb; «من» is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and «نجوى» is genitive by «من» in form and the fāʿil of «يكون» in position; «ثلاثة» is annexed to «نجوى» [as muḍāf ilayhi]. «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «رابعهم» the khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, so the exception is "emptied" (mufarragh) from the most general of states. «ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم» is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَلا أَدْنى مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ ما كانُوا): the wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negating; «أدنى» is conjoined to the form of «نجوى». It was also read in the nominative, conjoined to its position, and it was said: as a mubtadaʾ. «من ذلك» is attached to «أدنى»; «ولا أكثر» is conjoined to «ولا أدنى». «إلا» is a particle of restriction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «معهم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is circumstantial on the accusative reading or [the reading of] conjunction to the position, and a khabar of the mubtadaʾ on the nominative reading. «أينما» is an adverb of place attached to the settling to which «معهم» is attached, i.e. accompanying them with His knowledge in whatever place they settle. «كانوا» is a verb and its fāʿil, so it is the complete «كان», and the clause is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, because «ما» was added in it. It is also permissible that «ما» be maṣdar-forming, so that the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the particle-relative.
(ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence; «ينبئهم» is an imperfect verb, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil referring to Allah; «بما» is in the position of the second object; the clause «عملوا» has no grammatical position; «يوم القيامة» is attached to «ينبئهم»; [then] «إنّ» and its noun and its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلا هو رابعهم ولا خمسة إلا هو سادسهم ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر إلا هو معهم» there is the device of al-infiṣāl (extrication). Reference to it has preceded, and we repeat it here to complete the benefit. We say: it is a device whose gist is that the speaker says something against which an objection can be raised, and he does not stop at it until he brings what extricates him from that, either overtly or covertly, in a way that interpretation brings out. For against the apparent sense of this noble verse a number of questions can be raised, among them:
1- Why was beginning with two omitted in it, when that is the first rank among those who converse in secret?
2- Why did He move from three to five, departing from the order of moving from three to four?
3- Why did He not go beyond five as He went beyond three?
4- Why did He not say «من نجوى ثلاثة» and stop at that, making do with His saying after it «ولا أدنى من ذلك ولا أكثر», so that the lesser would cover two and the greater would cover four up to the endless numbers?
5- Why did He turn from the more concise to the longer, although the more concise fully conveys the intended meaning?
Before we explain the extrication from this, a historical glimpse must be mentioned, by which the veil is lifted. There is disagreement about the occasion of its revelation. It was said: the idolaters gathered in groups of these two numbers, three by three and five by five, conversing secretly about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, thinking that this was hidden from him; so it was revealed so that Allah would inform His Prophet of their state. It was also said: three men of Quraysh gathered one day — Rabīʿa and Ḥabīb, the two sons of ʿAmr, and Ṣafwān ibn Umayya — and were talking. One of them said: "Do you think Allah knows what we say?" Another said: "He knows some and does not know some." The third said: "If He knows some, then He knows all." So it was revealed. The exegetes have authenticated this second report.
Al-Zamakhsharī said, in answer to some of the objections to the apparent sense of the verse mentioned above, after quoting the occasion of revelation that we have mentioned: that the Creator, Mighty and Majestic — and He knows best — intended to mention the customary numbers of the people of secret conversation and the people of consultation; those delegated for that are not all the people, but only a select group of people of intellect and forbearance, and a band of people of experience and judgement; their number starts at two and goes up to six, as the situation requires and as sound judgement decides. Do you not see that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, left the consultation (shūrā) among six and did not go beyond them to a seventh? [Translator's note: what follows is the author's quotation of another critic (the wording matches Ibn Abī al-Iṣbaʿ in Taḥrīr al-Taḥbīr / Badīʿ al-Qur'an); the source does not name him here.] This is the text of al-Zamakhsharī's words; I have reported it in his wording, leaving nothing out of it and not replacing a word with a word. As for the first report he related, there is no difficulty in it and no objection against it. As for the second report, which was authenticated — it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him — the difficulty applies to it. As for al-Zamakhsharī's saying that the speech came according to the custom of the Arabs regarding the people of secret conversation and the people of consultation, because the number of these two groups does not exceed six; and as for his citing as evidence the case of ʿUmar and his putting the consultation among six, and his emphasising that by his saying "Do you not see that he did not go beyond six with the meaning of consultation to a seventh?" — I do not know where he got that from! How can his claim be valid that, in the custom of the Arabs, the people of secret conversation and the people of consultation are only of these two numbers and not other numbers, when the Mighty Qur'an has come with the opposite of that? Allah the Exalted said, informing about the sons of Yaʿqūb: «فلما استيأسوا منه خلصوا نجيا», and they were ten; so He, glorified is He, called their conversation secret conversing. And He, Mighty and Majestic, said, relating about the chiefs of Pharaoh: «وأسروا النجوى» «إن هذان لساحران», and they could not be counted for their multitude. And the Exalted said: «يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا ناجيتم الرسول فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة»; and those who converse privately with the Messenger could be two and upward to the full number of the Community, for the address is to all the believers, and He, glorified is He, did not restrict the number of those conversing to a definite amount. And He, glorified is He, said: «فلا تتناجوا بالإثم والعدوان ومعصية الرسول», not restricting that to a fixed number; and He, glorified is He, said: «وأمرهم شورى بينهم», with no definite number. Even though some of these verses were revealed about a specific incident, Allah sent down their meaning in general wording so as to include the whole Community, so the ruling in them is general. As for the case of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, it is known that he did not put the matter to consultation among those six out of regard for this number; he only had regard for those fit for the matter. The six among whom he placed the matter were the notables of the Companions and the best of those who remained after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and after the two shaykhs (Abū Bakr and ʿUmar), and the matter was not permitted to go outside them or pass beyond them to others. Had those fit for this matter been more than this number or fewer, he would have placed the matter among them, and would not have cared whether they fell short of this number or exceeded it.
What is fit to be an answer, by which one is extricated from the difficulty set out at the beginning of the discussion, is to say: those about whom the revelation of the verse is authentically reported are the three whom Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, named. Since this number, I mean three, is what is intended by the verse, it was mentioned first in it, before the last number, so that His concern with it would be known [Translator's note: the source has «ليعلم أئمتهم به», apparently a corruption of «ليُعلَم اهتمامه به»], for when the speaker has concern for something, he mentions it in his speech before other things in matters like these. Then He mentioned the lesser and the greater to remove the possibility that we presented earlier. If this is the incident because of which the verse was revealed, the first question falls away, in which it was said: why did He not mention the first rank of those who converse secretly, and make do with mentioning "the lesser" after mentioning three so as to cover two, or "the greater" to cover what is above three?
The answer to the saying "What is the benefit of mentioning five after mentioning three, when the saying of the Exalted «ولا أكثر» makes it and others up to the endless unnecessary?" is that He, glorified is He, wanted to teach us the manner of moving through these numbers, rising from three to five, so that it would be known that the reference is to all the ranks of numbers, and that the manner of moving in the rest is like the manner [of moving] to five. If it is said: "Then why was this teaching not by four, which was omitted? Mentioning it would have been more fitting, because moving from three to four is more correct than moving from three to five, for numbers coming in order is more correct than their coming out of order, and the purpose of teaching the manner of moving would have been achieved by that," I say: two things prevented that. One of them is the fear that the composition of the speech would come out faulty, because of its heaviness on the tongue and the ear, due to the ugliness of repeating the word for four with no barrier keeping one of the two words apart from the other. For if it were said «إلا هو رابعهم ولا أربعة», the speech would be heavy because of the adjacency of two words in which there are four letters of the throat, namely the two ʿayns and the two hāʾs. Al-Āmidī faulted Abū Tammām for the like of this in his saying:
كريم متى أمدحه أمدحه والورى ... معي وإذا ما لمته لمته وحدي
(A noble man: whenever I praise him, I praise him with all mankind joining me; and whenever I blame him, I blame him alone.)
and he called it muʿāẓala (entanglement), which is the most hideous of the faults that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb denied of the poetry of Zuhayr when he characterised it — although someone other than al-Āmidī counted muʿāẓala as something other than this. The second thing that prevented mentioning four is the eloquent composer's fleeing from repeating meanings and words without benefit. Had He moved to four, the ruling would have been repeated, because the ruling on it has already been given in five, for five is four and more, so four is included in it, and whatever rulings apply to it apply to four. Also, [there is] fleeing from mentioning the even and turning from it to mentioning the odd, because of the merits that make the odd deserve mention rather than the even, which others do not have. In this answer given to the second question there is an answer to the third question. As for the answer to the fourth question, namely his saying: "Why did He not move from five to seven as He moved from three to five and end at that limit, instead of neglecting this number which is distinguished by properties Allah the Exalted placed in it, because of which the number of the heavens and the earth, the days of time, the climes of the earth, and things there is no room to mention came in accordance with it?" — we say: the intention was to teach the manner of moving, and that was achieved by mentioning five; so repeating it with another number is a useless lengthening made unnecessary by what preceded it. If the properties of seven were regarded, it would be necessary to regard the properties of nine as well. The intention of the verse is not to draw attention to the properties of numbers; the intention is only what we have mentioned. Otherwise, whenever the properties of numbers are considered, you will find five distinguished by what no other number is distinguished by. Among its properties in which it is unique is that it is the first number that gathers three odd numbers: one, three and five; and among them is that the number of its odd numbers is odd, and this does not belong to any other among all the numbers of the rank of units, nor to what is built on its basis and branches from it. For three gathers only two odd numbers, and the number of its odd numbers is likewise even. As for seven, even though it gathers four odd numbers, the number of its odd numbers is even, and it is compound in relation to five, because it is five and more, while five is simple in relation to it, and the simple is the root of the compound. Nine, even though it gathers more than seven and the number of its odd numbers comes out odd, is compound in relation to seven, which is compound in relation to five; so five, in relation to it, is the root of the root. Since five has this standing, mentioning it was more fitting than mentioning seven, and it had to be brought in order to draw attention to the honour and excellence it has over others, and one must stop at it and limit the teaching of the manner of moving to it. By this it is established that the composition of the verse as it came is more eloquent than what the one raising the question and the one singling out the difficulty imagined.
Al-Karkhī said: "He singled out three and five for mention because a group of the hypocrites stayed behind to converse secretly, and they were of the number mentioned, to vex the believers; so the verse was revealed with a description of their state and as a making known of them. Or because the odd number is nobler than the even, since Allah the Exalted is odd (witr) and loves the odd; so the two numbers mentioned were singled out for mention to draw attention to the fact that divine matters must be observed in all matters. Then after mentioning them, what is added to them covers others among those who converse secretly."
Al-Khāzin has a fine passage that we quote as follows to complete the discussion. He said: "If you say: why did He single out three and five? I say: because the least that suffices in consultation is three, so that the purpose is achieved: two are like disputants over the negative and the affirmative, and the third is like the mediator judging between them; then consultation is praiseworthy and the purpose is achieved. Likewise every group that gathers for consultation must have one who is an arbiter among them whose word is accepted. It was also said that the odd number is nobler than the even; for this reason Allah the Exalted singled out three and five."

dervis-irab:8-10.t:
* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ نُهُوا عَنِ النَّجْوى ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ): resumptive speech, set forth to explain another pattern of their secret conversation and their winking among themselves — they being the Jews and the hypocrites — whenever they saw the believers, intending by that to provoke them and inflame their anger. The Prophet ﷺ often forbade them from that, but they would hardly desist before returning to the like of what they had done. The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīr); «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «تر» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "أنت"; «إلى الذين» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تر». The clause «نهوا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «نهوا» is a passive past verb and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); «عن النجوى» is attached to «نهوا». «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «يعودون» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ). He turned away from the past form suited to the conjunction for a subtle secret, namely calling to mind the image of the returning, its renewal and its embodiment. «لما» is attached to «يعودون»; the clause «نهوا» is the ṣila; «عنه» is attached to «نهوا».
(وَيَتَناجَوْنَ بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «يتناجون» is an imperfect verb conjoined to «يعودون» — and in the imperfect form there is what was just mentioned of embodiment, calling to mind and renewal. «بالإثم» is attached to «يتناجون»; «العدوان» is conjoined to «الإثم», and «معصية الرسول» is also conjoined.
