Some of those who hold to the literal sense (al-ẓāhir) said: expiation is not obligatory upon him until he pronounces ẓihār a second time, and they related that from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ashajj. Qatāda said: ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما قالُوا is that after the ẓihār he resolves to have intercourse with her and to approach her. Some of the jurists said: his return is that he keeps her and does not divorce her after the ẓihār, so the expiation becomes obligatory upon him. Al-Qutabī said: it is that he returns to what used to be said in the Jāhiliyya. Abū l-ʿĀliya said: لِما قالُوا i.e. concerning what they said. Al-Farrāʾ said: لما قالوا, إلى ما قالوا and فيما قالوا are one and the same; he means: they go back on their statement. Al-Akhfash said: there is a fronting and a postponement in it, i.e. "then the freeing of a slave for what they said". Among the clearest of them is the view of Qatāda, i.e. then they return to the prohibition which they had uttered and make it lawful. فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ, or "then upon them is the freeing of a slave"; and according to the Basran grammarians فتحرير رقبة is permissible [Translator's note: presumably in the accusative, فَتَحْرِيرَ رَقَبَةٍ, i.e. "then let them free…"; the printed text does not show the vowelling]. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا: before the man touches the woman, and before the woman touches the man. This is general, except that Sufyān used to say: [it is permitted] to him what is short of intercourse.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
مِنْ [Translator's note: i.e. مَن] is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "so whoever does not find the slave" — and the object is omitted when the meaning is known — "then upon him is the fasting of two months". صيام شهرين [Translator's note: presumably with tanwīn, ṣiyāmun shahrayni] is permissible on the basis that شهرين is an adverb (ẓarf); and if you wish it is an object by way of extension (ʿalā l-saʿa). But when you say صيام شهرين [Translator's note: i.e. in construct], it cannot be an adverb. On this basis Sībawayh related, among [verbs] that pass over to two objects: [Rajaz] 470-
يا سارق اللّيلة أهل الدار
(O you who rob the people of the house tonight)
 فَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَإِطْعامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِيناً i.e. whoever is unable to fast because of old age or chronic illness, then upon him is the feeding of sixty poor people; and tanwīn on إطعام is permissible. "Before they touch one another" is not [stated] here, but it is taken from consensus. ذلك ليؤمنوا بالله ورسوله [Translator's note: so in the source; the muṣḥaf has ذلِكَ لِتُؤْمِنُوا]: Abū Isḥāq said: i.e. that severity; and someone else said: We did that so that you would believe in Allah and His Messenger, i.e. so that you would affirm what has come to you and so believe. وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ i.e. these are the obligations of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, which He has delimited. وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ i.e. for whoever disbelieves in them.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ i.e. they oppose Allah and His Messenger and place themselves in the boundary (ḥadd) of His enemies.
كُبِتُوا i.e. they were enraged; and some of the lexicographers said: i.e. they perished. He said: and the original is كبدوا, from their saying كبده when he struck him with a pain in his liver (kabid). كَما كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ: the kāf is in the position of an accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar (verbal noun). ولهم عذاب مهين [Translator's note: so in the source; the muṣḥaf has وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ مُهِينٌ].

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ: what governs يوم is «عذاب». According to the Basrans it may not be indeclinable (mabnī) when an imperfect verb comes after it; it is only made indeclinable when a past verb or something not declinable comes after it — when it is like that, it is made indeclinable, because since it needs what comes after it and cannot do without it, it is treated like it. As for the Kufans, they say: it is made indeclinable only because it has the meaning of إذا, so it is made indeclinable because of its [i.e. إذا's] indeclinability. جَمِيعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. on the day when Allah raises them from their graves to the Resurrection in the state of being gathered together. فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا i.e. He informs them of what they kept secret and concealed and other than those two among their deeds. أَحْصاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ i.e. He counted it, recorded it and preserved it, while those who did it forgot it. وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ i.e. over everything of their deeds a witness, knowing it.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: I.e. have you not seen with the eye of your heart, so that you know that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, nothing small or great being hidden from Him — so how could the deeds of these people be hidden from Him? ما يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوى ثَلاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān said, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: He, the Exalted, is above His Throne, and His knowledge is with them. ثلاثة is genitive as a badal (substitute) for «نجوى»; it may be genitive by the annexation of نجوى to it; it may be nominative according to the position of نجوى; and it may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun that is in نجوى. إِلَّا هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. Al-Farrāʾ related that in the codex (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] there is ولا أربعة إلّا هو خامسهم, and Abū Ḥātim related that in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh there is: ما يكون من نجوى ثلاثة إلّا الله رابعهم ولا خمسة إلّا الله سادسهم ولا أقلّ من ذلك ولا أكثر إلّا الله معهم إذا انتجوا. Abū Jaʿfar said: this reading, if it is authentic, is only by way of explanation (tafsīr); it may not be recited except on that basis. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read ما تكون من نجوى ثلاثة; this reading, even though it differs from the authority of the majority, agrees with the written text (al-sawād) and is permissible in Arabic, because نجوى is feminine in form and «من» in it is redundant (zāʾida), just as you say: ما جاءني من رجل and ما جاءتني من امرأة. The implied form is: "and there is no secret conversation of four but He is the fifth of them". Hārūn related from ʿAmr from al-Ḥasan that he read وَلا أَدْنى مِنْ ذلِكَ وَلا أَكْثَرَ [Translator's note: i.e. وَلا أَكْثَرُ in the nominative, as the following remark implies; the print does not show it] إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ, conjoining it to the position. ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِما عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ i.e. then He will inform them of what they conversed secretly about. إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ of their secret conversations and their confidences and their other deeds and the deeds of His servants.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t:
Mujāhid said: they are a group of the Jews. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read ينتاجون بالإثم والعدوان [Translator's note: so printed; Ḥamza's reading is known as يَنْتَجُونَ]; and يتناجون is clearer, because they have agreed on reading إذا تناجيتم فلا تتناجوا — except for something narrated from Ibn Masʿūd, that he also read وينتجون بالإثم والعدوان وعصيان الرسول [Translator's note: so in the source; the muṣḥaf has وَمَعْصِيَتِ الرَّسُولِ]. وَإِذا جاؤُكَ حَيَّوْكَ بِما لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ: Abū Jaʿfar said: we have already mentioned its meaning. وَيَقُولُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَوْلا يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ بِما نَقُولُ i.e. why does He not punish us for that at the time we say it? حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَها فَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ: a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. The grammarians related that one says:
حسبك, and no khabar is pronounced for it because its meaning is known; and it is said: it carries the meaning of a command, because its meaning is "refrain"; so since a command is not given a khabar, the khabar of what has its meaning was omitted.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا تَناجَيْتُمْ فَلا تَتَناجَوْا بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ: there are three ways in it: فلا تتناجوا with two tāʾs; ولا تناجوا with a single tāʾ; and ولا تناجوا with the tāʾ assimilated into the tāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. فَلَا تَنَّاجَوْا; the print does not show the doubling]. Whoever brings it with two tāʾs says: it is a word begun with, separate from what is before it. Whoever brings it with one tāʾ omitted [one] because of the meeting of the two tāʾs, like تذكرون and تتذكّرون. Whoever assimilates says: two identical letters have met with an alif before them, and an assimilated letter may come after an alif, as in دواب. وَتَناجَوْا بِالْبِرِّ i.e. with what brings you near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty. وَالتَّقْوى i.e. with fearing Him by performing His obligations and avoiding what He has forbidden. وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ الَّذِي إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ i.e. to whom is your destination and your gathering, so He will recompense you for your deeds.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
إِنَّمَا النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ: the soundest of what has been said about it is the view of Qatāda. He said: the hypocrites used to converse secretly in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, and that would grieve the Muslims and weigh heavily upon them, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down: إِنَّمَا النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ لِيَحْزُنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا, the verse. What shows the correctness of this view is the Qurʾān before it and after it. Ibn Zayd said: a man would converse privately with the Prophet ﷺ about a need, and he would do that so that people would see that he had conversed privately with the Prophet ﷺ; then Iblīs would whisper to the Muslims, saying: "This private conversation is only about forces that have gathered against you and some matter that has come up which is intended against you", so they would grieve at that. There is a third view on the verse, mentioned by Muḥammad ibn Jarīr. He said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Wāḍiḥ narrated to us, saying:
Yaḥyā ibn Dāwūd al-Bajalī narrated to us, saying: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī was asked, while I was listening, about dreams, and he said: dreams are of three ranks. Among them is what Satan whispers, and that is the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: إِنَّمَا النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ لِيَحْزُنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا; among them is what a man tells himself and then sees in his sleep; and among them is a taking by the hand. And it is read لِيَحْزُنَ [Translator's note: i.e. the alternative vowelling, لِيَحْزُنَ vs. لِيُحْزِنَ, which the print does not distinguish], and the first is more eloquent. وَلَيْسَ بِضارِّهِمْ شَيْئاً إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: i.e. by the decree and determination of Allah; and it is said: بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ — by what Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has permitted in it, namely their distress over the believers, because He, exalted be His praise, has permitted that. وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ i.e. let them entrust their affair to Him, and let not the secret conversation and what the hypocrites confide to one another grieve them, since Allah, Majestic and Mighty, protects them and guards them.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: في المجلس: it is narrated from al-Ḥasan and Qatāda that they both read إذا قيل لكم تفاسحوا. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is like تعهدت ضيعتي and تعاهدت. The lexicographers said: تعهّدت is more eloquent because it is an act by one person; and al-Khalīl said: one only says تعهّدت because it is an act by one person. Al-Ḥasan and ʿĀṣim read فِي الْمَجالِسِ, and the reading of the generality is في المجلس. Abū Jaʿfar said: the scholars disagreed about its meaning. It is authentically reported from Mujāhid that he said: it is the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ specifically; and it is authentically reported from Qatāda that he said: people used to vie with one another in the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ, hardly any of them making room for another, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down this, meaning that. It is narrated from Qatāda that it concerns the gathering of remembrance (majlis al-dhikr); and al-Ḥasan and Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb said: this is about fighting specifically. Abū Jaʿfar said: the apparent sense of the verse is general, so it must be taken accordingly, and this will then apply to the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ specifically, to war and to gatherings of remembrance — and we know of no fourth view; and the meaning conveys the meaning of "assemblies" (majālis). Moreover, when a person is addressed to make room in his seat and with him is a group who have been commanded with what he was commanded, they have become assemblies. يَفْسَحِ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ is the response to the command, and it carries the meaning of requital (al-mujāzāh). And a فسيح place, i.e. a spacious one. وَإِذا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ and Shayba; and the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and the people of Kufa is انْشُزُوا فَانْشُزُوا [Translator's note: the two readings are unshuzū (with ḍamma) and inshizū (with kasra); the print does not distinguish them]. They are two dialects with one meaning, and Abū ʿUbayd prefers the second. If a preference could occur in this, the ḍamma would be more fitting, because it is an intransitive verb like قعد يقعد, since most commonly in the speech of the Arabs what is intransitive comes with ḍamma, and what is transitive comes with kasra, like ضرب يضرب. As for the meaning, the soundest of what has been said about it is that it is rising up to every good: commanding right and forbidding wrong, or fighting an enemy, or dispersing from the Prophet ﷺ so that no harm reaches him. يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجاتٍ: it is said: i.e. He raises them in reward and honour; and it is said: He raises them, from elevation, i.e. He raises them above others who do not know, in order to make their excellence clear. وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ i.e. He is informed of it and will requite it.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: they had troubled the Prophet ﷺ with the great number of their private consultations, so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, wished to lighten [the burden] on him and commanded them with this; so they held back from private consultation. Then He made it broad for them and did not make it narrow. Mujāhid said: no one acted upon this verse except ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him: he gave a dīnār in charity and then consulted the Prophet ﷺ privately; then it was abrogated. And he [ʿAlī], may the mercy of Allah be upon him, said: through me [the burden] was lightened for this community. The Prophet ﷺ said to me: "What do you think — should whoever consults privately give a dīnār in charity?" I said: "No." He said: "Then a dirham?" I said: "No." He said: "How much, then?" I said: "A grain of barley." He said: "You are indeed one who asks little (zahīd)." Then the lightening was sent down. فَإِنْ لَمْ تَجِدُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ i.e. He does not burden one who does not find [the means].

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: The origin of al-ishfāq in the language is caution and fear; and because of this it is not lawful for anyone to describe Allah, Majestic and Mighty, with ishfāq, nor to say: "O Shafīq". Mujāhid said: أأشفقتم i.e. did it weigh hard upon you? فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا وَتابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ: so since He has turned to you [in forgiveness], He did not hold them to account. فأقيموا الصلاة وآتوا الزكاة i.e. then do that whose obligation has not been lifted from you. وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ i.e. in what He has commanded you. وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ i.e. and He will requite you for it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا قَوْماً غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ i.e. have you not looked with the eye of your heart and seen them? ما هُمْ مِنْكُمْ وَلا مِنْهُمْ: the pronoun refers back to الذين, and they are the hypocrites: they are not of the believers, i.e. of the people of their religion and creed, nor of those with whom Allah is angry, and they are the Jews. وَيَحْلِفُونَ عَلَى الْكَذِبِ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ: they swear that they are believers.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: ما is in the position of a nominative, i.e. evil is the thing which they do, namely their deceiving the believers and their sincere counsel to the disbelievers.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: اتَّخَذُوا أَيْمانَهُمْ جُنَّةً i.e. they took their swearing to the believers that they are of them as a barrier for their blood and their property. And this is the meaning of فَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ, because the way of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, regarding the idolaters is that they be fought, and regarding the People of the Book that they be fought unless they pay the jizya; so when these people displayed faith while being disbelievers, they turned the believers away from fighting them by what they displayed.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: I.e. you will not benefit from wealth so as to ransom yourselves with it [Translator's note: so in the source, in the second person], and their children will not benefit them so as to help them and rescue them from the punishment they are in. أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ: the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is permissible outside the Qurʾān.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ i.e. they will swear to Him upon falsehood; and this is a clear proof of the falsity of the view of whoever said: no one will speak on the Day of Resurrection except the truth, because of what he witnesses.
وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ i.e. on something that benefits them. أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ: إنّ is with kasra because it is at the start [of a sentence]; and I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān permit it with fatḥa, because the meaning of ألا is "truly" (ḥaqqan).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ فَأَنْساهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ: this is among what has come in its original form; had it come with the weakening (iʿlāl) [of the weak letter], it would have been استحاذ, just as one says: استصاب فلان رأي فلان, and one does not say استصوب. Abū Jaʿfar said: what comes in its original form is only among what is taken by hearing from the Arabs, not among what is used as a basis for analogy. And it is said: the four-letter [i.e. derived] verb is weakened following the three-letter one; so since one says استحوذ عليه when he overcomes him, and does not say حاذ with this meaning — one only says حاذ الإبل when he gathers the camels — since it has no three-letter [counterpart], it came in its original form.
أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطانِ أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ الشَّيْطانِ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ: his party (ḥizb) is his allies, his followers and his hosts; and the loser (al-khāsir) is the one who has lost in his bargain.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحَادُّونَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ: Qatāda said: they show enmity to Him; Mujāhid said: they oppose [Him]; and it is said:
its meaning is: they contravene the limits (ḥudūd) of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in what He has commanded. Its literal sense in Arabic is: they come to be in a boundary (ḥadd) other than His boundary which He has delimited. The original is يحاددون, and the dāl was assimilated into the dāl. أُولئِكَ فِي الْأَذَلِّينَ i.e. among those whom abasement overtakes; and أولئك and what follows is the khabar (predicate) of الذين.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي: it is said: i.e. He wrote in the Preserved Tablet; and al-Farrāʾ made it figurative, making كتب have the meaning of «قال», i.e. Allah [said]: I will surely prevail, I and My messengers, i.e. over whoever opposes Us. «ورسلي» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the implied pronoun that is in «لأغلبن», and «أنا» is a tawkīd (emphasis). Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the eloquent usage. All the grammarians permitted in poetry: لأقومنّ وزيد [Translator's note: i.e. conjoining to the nominative pronoun without an emphasizing pronoun]. The Kufans and a group of the theorists permitted conjoining to the nominative implied pronoun without tawkīd, because it occurs both attached and detached, and so differs from the genitive implied pronoun. إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ i.e. possessor of strength and power to [carry out] what He wrote concerning whoever opposes Him and opposes His messengers. عَزِيزٌ in His retribution; no one is able to avenge himself on Him.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
The soundest of what has been narrated about this is that it was revealed concerning the hypocrites who befriended the Jews, because they do not acknowledge Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in the way He must be acknowledged, nor do they believe in the Last Day so as to fear punishment. يُوادُّونَ is in the position of an accusative because it is the [second object, i.e.] khabar of تجد, or a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. وَلَوْ كانُوا آباءَهُمْ أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ i.e. even if those who opposed Allah and His Messenger were their fathers. [آباء is] the plural of أب according to the original [form]; its original is أبو, and the dual is also according to the original among the Basrans and nothing else, while the Kufans related: جاءني أبان. أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ is the plural of ابن according to the original; its original is بني, what has dropped from it being a yāʾ, while what has dropped from أب is a wāw. As for أب, the dual indicates it; as for ابن, the derivation indicates it.
Abū Isḥāq said: it is derived from "his father built him" (بناه أبوه), يبنيه [Translator's note: printed يبينه]. Abū Jaʿfar said: some of the grammarians erred and said: what dropped from it is a wāw, because البنوّة (sonship) has been heard. أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ is the plural of أخ according to the original, just as you say ورل and ورلان. أُولئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْإِيمانَ: it is said: it is figurative, and «في» has the meaning of the lām, i.e. He wrote faith for their hearts, it being known that the meaning is "He wrote for them"; and it is said: it is literal, i.e. He wrote in their hearts the mark of faith so that it is known that they are believers. وَأَيَّدَهُمْ بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ: it is said: with light and guidance; and it is said: with Jibrāʾīl ﷺ, who helps them, supports them and grants them success. وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها as a ḥāl (circumstantial). رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ i.e. for their obedience in this world. وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ for His admitting them into Paradise. أُولئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ i.e. His army and His company; and تحزّب القوم [means] the people gathered together. أَلا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ: it is said: i.e. those who attained what they wanted.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). (في زوجها) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تجادلك), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "في شأن زوجها" (concerning the matter of her husband). (إلى اللَّه) attached to (تشتكي)..
The clause «قد سمع اللَّه ...» has no grammatical position, being initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «تجادلك ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «تشتكي ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause تجادلك.. [Note: It may be the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هي", and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).].
The clause «اللَّه يسمع ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the initial clause.
The clause «يسمع ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (اللَّه).
The clause «إنّ اللَّه سميع ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(تحاور) a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the five-letter verb تحاور; its pattern is تفاعل, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the ʿayn..

* Benefits:
- The ruling on ẓihār..
From ʿĀʾisha, who said: Praise be to Allah whose hearing encompasses all voices. The woman who disputed, Khawla bint Thaʿlaba, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and spoke to him in a corner of the house, and I could not hear what she was saying; then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِها وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ.
Her husband was Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit; he had sought intercourse with her and she refused him, so he said to her: "You are to me like my mother's back." So she came disputing with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning her husband. As for the ruling on one who pronounces ẓihār, expiation (kaffāra) becomes obligatory upon him. The verse indicates that expiation is obligatory before touching; if he has intercourse before he expiates, only one expiation is obligatory upon him, and this is the view of most of the people of knowledge, such as Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad and Sufyān. As for the expiation of ẓihār, it is in a fixed order: he must free a believing slave; whoever does not find one, then a fast of two consecutive months. If he breaks the fast on one day deliberately, or forgets the intention, he must restart the two months. If he has intercourse at night during the fast he has sinned by that, but he is not required to restart the two months. If he is unable to fast, because of illness, old age, or excessive desire that does not allow him to refrain from intercourse, he must feed sixty poor persons, each poor person a mudd of the staple food of the land, of wheat, barley, rice, sorghum or dates. If he gave the sixty ṣāʿs to a single poor person, that would not suffice according to al-Shāfiʿī, by the apparent meaning of the verse, while Abū Ḥanīfa permitted that — may Allah be pleased with them both. If he has a slave whom he needs for service, or he has the price of a slave but needs it for maintenance, he turns to fasting. And Allah knows best.
[Translator's note: The source says "the sixty ṣāʿs", although it had just specified a mudd for each poor person.]

safi-cedvel:2-4.t:
* I'rab:
(منكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of يظاهرون. (من نسائهم) attached to (يظاهرون). (ما) negative, operating as ليس operates. (إن) a particle of negation. (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr). (اللائي) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أمّهاتهم). (الواو) a conjunction. (اللام) for emphasis. (منكرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من القول) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of (منكرا). (الواو) a conjunction. (اللام) for emphasis..
The clause «الذين يظاهرون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive. The clause «يظاهرون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ما هنّ أمّهاتهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «إن أمّهاتهم إلّا اللائي ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya). The clause «ولدنهم ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (اللائي).
The clause «إنّهم ليقولون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّ الله لعفوّ ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause إنّهم ليقولون.
3- (الواو) a conjunction, and likewise (ثمّ). (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause after it is the ṣila.]. (الفاء) redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar, because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to a condition. (تحرير) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "عليهم" (upon them). (من قبل) attached to (تحرير). (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما قالوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يعودون).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يتماسّا..) is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(ذلكم) a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the ruling mentioned. (الواو) in (توعظون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (به) attached to (توعظون), by its being made to imply (taḍmīn) the meaning of "تزجرون" (you are restrained). (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.]..
The clause «الذين يظاهرون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the first clause الذين يظاهرون.
The clause «يظاهرون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يعودون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «(عليهم) تحرير ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يتماسّا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «ذلكم توعظون به» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
The clause «توعظون به» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ذلكم).
The clause «الله ... خبير» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تعملون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second particle-relative (ما).
4- (الفاء) resumptive. (من) a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. (لم) for negation only [Note: According to most of those who parse it, it is what makes the following verb jussive, but we have preferred the parsing above so that the speech retains its indication of the future.]. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (صيام) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "عليه" (upon him). (من قبل أن يتماسّا) like the first, the adverb being attached to (صيام). (الفاء) a conjunction. (من لم يستطع) like من لم يجد. (فإطعام) like فصيام. (مسكينا) tamyīz (specification), accusative. The reference in (ذلك) is to the explanation and instruction, and it is a mubtadaʾ [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being "فعلنا ذلك" (We did that).] whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being "واقع" (taking place). (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl). (تؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تؤمنوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to the omitted khabar [Note: Or attached to the omitted verb.].
(بالله) attached to (تؤمنوا). (الواو) a conjunction in the two places. The reference in (تلك) is to the rulings mentioned. (للكافرين) attached to an advanced khabar of the mubtadaʾ (عذاب)..
The clause «من لم يجد ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لم يجد ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «(عليه) صيام ...» is in the position of the jussive (fī maḥall jazm) as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يتماسّا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «من لم يستطع ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause من لم يجد.
The clause «لم يستطع ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.]. The clause «(عليه) إطعام ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ذلك (واقع) ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تؤمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «تلك حدود ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «للكافرين عذاب ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the last resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(4) متتابعين: dual of متتابع, an active participle of the five-letter verb تتابع; its pattern is متفاعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(ستين) a noun of number, one of the words for the decades; its pattern is فعلين, and its ʿayn and lām came from a single letter.

* Rhetoric:
Negation and affirmation (al-salb wa-l-ījāb): in His saying, Exalted is He: الَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ نِسائِهِمْ ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ إِنْ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّائِي وَلَدْنَهُمْ.
This device is the negation of a thing from one aspect and its affirmation from another aspect, or commanding a thing from one aspect and forbidding it from a second aspect.
Here, in this noble verse, there is a negation of the woman's becoming a mother through ẓihār, and an affirmation of motherhood for the one who gave birth to the child.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) in (كبتوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle. (من قبلهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of الذين..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كبت..) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)..
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). (للكافرين عذاب) its i'rab has preceded [Note: In the previous verse (4).].
The clause «إنّ الذين ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحادّون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «كبتوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «كبت ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «أنزلنا ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «للكافرين عذاب ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
6- (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (مهين) [Note: Or attached to the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) to which (للكافرين) is attached.]. (جميعا) a ḥāl from the absent pronoun in (يبعثهم) [Note: Or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the pronoun, accusative.]. (الفاء) a conjunction. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.]. (على كلّ) attached to the khabar (شهيد).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (ينبّئهم).
The clause «يبعثهم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ينبّئهم ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يبعثهم.
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «أحصاه الله ...» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «نسوه ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the causal clause [Note: It may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in أحصاه, with قد implied.].
The clause «الله ... شهيد» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the causal clause.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation. (في السموات) attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and likewise (في الأرض).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله يعلم..) is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of ترى.
(ما) negative. (يكون) a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb. (نجوى) genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil (agent) of يكون. (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr) in the three places. (لا) redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation in the three following places. (خمسة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to نجوى, following it in the genitive in form [Note: Or conjoined to the number ثلاثة.. And (أدنى) may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is the clause هو معهم, the conjunction then being a conjoining of clauses..], and likewise (أدنى وأكثر). (من ذلك) attached to (أدنى). (معهم) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هو). (أينما) an adverb of place stripped of the conditional sense, attached to the notion of settledness (al-istiqrār) to which معهم is attached. (كانوا) a complete past verb and its agent. (ثمّ) a conjunction. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.].
The interpreted maṣdar (ما عملوا..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (ينبّئهم).
(يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (ينبّئهم). (بكلّ) attached to the khabar (عليم).
The clause «تر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يعلم ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «ما يكون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive, to confirm the content of what preceded.
The clause «هو رابعهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «هو سادسهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «هو معهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «كانوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ينبّئهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ما يكون.
The clause «عملوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «إنّ الله ... عليم» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

* Rhetoric:
Singling out three and five: in His saying, Exalted is He: ما يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوى ثَلاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رابِعُهُمْ وَلا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سادِسُهُمْ.
What calls for singling out three and five is that He, Glorified is He, intended to mention what custom has run upon regarding the numbers of those who hold private counsel. Those entrusted with consultation and delegated to it are not just anyone; rather they are a chosen group of the people of intellect and forbearance, and a band of the people of judgement and experience. Their number starts at two and rises to five, to six, to whatever the situation requires. Do you not see how ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him, left the matter as a consultation among six and did not go beyond them to a seventh? So He, Mighty and Exalted, mentioned three and five, and said «وَلا أَدْنى مِنْ ذلِكَ», which indicates two and four, and said «وَلا أَكْثَرَ», which indicates what follows and approaches this number.

safi-cedvel:8-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى الذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترى) in the meaning of "تنظر" (look), and the wāw in (نهوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (عن النجوى) attached to (نهوا). (لما) attached to (يعودون). (عنه) attached to (نهوا). (الواو) a conjunction in the five places. (بالإثم) attached to (يتناجون). (حيّوك) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent) and (الكاف) the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (بما) attached to (حيّوك). (به) attached to (يحيّك). (في أنفسهم) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of يقولون, i.e. "keeping it secret". (لولا) a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted.]. (الفاء) resumptive, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being "هي", i.e. Hell.
The clause «تر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «نهوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «يعودون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «نهوا (the second)» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يتناجون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause يعودون.
The clause «جاؤوك ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «حيّوك ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لم يحيّك به الله ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative noun (ما).
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «يعذّبنا الله ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «نقول ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما نقول..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يعذّبنا).
The clause «حسبهم جهنّم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يصلونها ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl [Note: Or parenthetical, if the clause (بئس المصير) is conjoined to the clause (حسبهم جهنّم).].
The clause «بئس المصير» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(نهوا) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by making vowelless (taskīn) and iʿlāl by deletion; its origin is نهيوا, with kasra on the hāʾ and ḍamma on the yāʾ. Then the yāʾ was made vowelless because of the heaviness of the ḍamma and the vowel was transferred to the hāʾ before it — iʿlāl by taskīn — then the yāʾ was deleted because it met, vowelless, with the wāw of the plural, so it became نهوا; its pattern is فعوا.
(معصية) an aural (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral عصى يعصي; its pattern is مفعلة, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. The tāʾ has been written open in the Muṣḥaf. The word may be a mīmī maṣdar..
(حيّوك) contains iʿlāl by deletion, because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and what precedes the wāw has fatḥa as an indication of the deleted alif; its pattern is فعّوك, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the doubled ʿayn.
(يحيّك) contains iʿlāl by deletion in keeping with the jussive; its pattern is يفعّك..

* Benefits:
- The cunning of the Jews..
From ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Al-sām (death) be upon you." ʿĀʾisha said: I understood it, and said: "Upon you be death and the curse."
She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Gently, O ʿĀʾisha; Allah loves gentleness in every matter." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, did you not hear what they said?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I said: And upon you."
In al-Bukhārī's version, the Jews came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Al-sām be upon you," and he said: "And upon you." ʿĀʾisha said: "Death be upon you, and may Allah curse you and be angry with you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O ʿĀʾisha, hold to gentleness, and beware of harshness and obscenity." She said: "Did you not hear what they said?" He said: "Did you not hear what I said? I returned it to them; it will be answered for me concerning them, and it will not be answered for them concerning me."
The meaning of al-sām is death. Al-Khaṭṭābī said: The generality of the ḥadīth scholars narrate: "When the People of the Book greet you, they only say: Al-sām be upon you; so say: And upon you."

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(أيّها) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative. (الذين) a badal (substitute) for أيّ, in the position of the accusative — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing. (بالإثم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تتناجوا). (بالبرّ) attached to (تناجوا). (إليه) attached to (تحشرون), and (الواو) in it is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The vocative clause «النداء ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «امنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «تناجيتم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا تتناجوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تناجوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «اتّقوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «تحشرون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
10- (إنّما) a restraining particle and the restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa). (من الشيطان) attached to the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (النجوى). (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl). (يحزن) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied (muḍmara) أن after the lām. (الذين) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent) [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the agent being a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to Satan.. حزنه يحزنه is of the class of نصر, and أحزنه means "he made him sad"..]. (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (ضارّهم) genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ليس, and the noun of ليس is a pronoun referring to Satan. (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "something of harm". (إلّا) for exception. (بإذن) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of the omitted excepted noun, i.e. "except a harm occurring by Allah's permission"..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحزن..) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted second khabar of النجوى.
(الواو) a conjunction. (على الله) attached to (يتوكّل). (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of an implied condition» [Translator's note: A stray closing quotation mark stands here in the source, apparently the remnant of a footnote marker.]. (اللام) the lām of command. (يتوكّل) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters..
The clause «النجوى من الشيطان ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يحزن ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «ليس بضارّهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «يتوكّل المؤمنون» is in the position of the jussive (fī maḥall jazm) as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: "If people rely on other than Allah, then let the believers rely on Allah".. And the clause of the condition and apodosis is conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative, made up of the condition إذا and its verb.

* Morphology:
(9) تتناجوا: contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, because of the meeting of the vowelless alif, the lām (third radical) of the verb, with the wāw of the plural; its pattern is تتفاعوا. (تناجوا) contains iʿlāl by deletion like تتناجوا and on its analogy.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has preceded [Note: Word by word and clause by clause, in verse (9) of the sūra.]. (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قيل). (في المجالس) attached to (تفسحوا). (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) in the two places. (يفسح) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the response to the imperative, vowelled with kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. The second (لكم) is attached to (يفسح). (يرفع) like يفسح. (منكم) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of آمنوا. (العلم) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) [Note: The wāw, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), is the first object.]. (درجات) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being of the kind of an adjective for it, i.e. "a raising possessed of degrees" [Note: Or a ḥāl with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "possessors of degrees".]. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause is the ṣila.].
[Translator's note: The source cites the verb here as (تفسحوا), while the clause list below has «تفسّحوا»; the Quranic word is تَفَسَّحُوا.]
The clause «قيل ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تفسّحوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil "1".
The clause «افسحوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «يفسح الله ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «قيل (the second)» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «انشزوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil "2".
[Translator's note: The markers "1" and "2" are footnote numbers in the source whose footnote texts are not included.]
The clause «يرفع الله ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the (second) relative noun (الذين).
The clause «الله ... خبير» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تعملون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).

* Morphology:
(المجالس) plural of المجلس, a noun of place from (جلس), of the class of ضرب; its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
Generalisation and specification (al-taʿmīm wa-l-takhṣīṣ): in His saying, Exalted is He: يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ دَرَجاتٍ.
In this noble verse there is generalisation followed by specification. That is because the recompense of raising in degrees here suits the deed: what was commanded was making room in the assembly, so that they would not compete for nearness to the elevated place around him ﷺ and crowd one another. Since the one who complies with that lowers himself from the elevation for which people compete, out of compliance and humility, he is recompensed for his humility by being raised in degrees, as in his saying: "Whoever humbles himself for Allah, Allah raises him." Then, since it is known that the people of knowledge are such that, in their own eyes and in the eyes of people, they merit elevated seats, He singled them out for mention at the recompense, so that it would be easy for them to give up the elevation they have in the assembly, out of humility to Allah the Exalted.

* Benefits:
- The excellence of knowledge..
Al-Ḥasan said: Ibn Masʿūd recited this verse and said: "O people, understand this verse, and let it make you desire knowledge, for Allah the Exalted says: He raises the knowledgeable believer above the believer who is not knowledgeable by degrees." And it has been said: the scholar attains through his knowledge a rank and elevation that others do not attain.
From Qays ibn Kathīr, who said: A man came from Medina to Abū al-Dardāʾ while he was in Damascus. He said: "What has brought you, my brother?" He said: "A ḥadīth that has reached me that you narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." He said:
"You have not come for some other need?" He said: "No." He said: "Have you not come for trade?" He said: "No." He said: "You have come only in search of this ḥadīth?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: Whoever travels a path seeking knowledge in it, Allah makes him travel by it a path to Paradise. The angels lower their wings out of pleasure with the seeker of knowledge, and those in the heavens and those on the earth seek forgiveness for the scholar, even the fish in the water. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon over all the other stars. The scholars are the heirs of the prophets, and the prophets did not leave dīnār or dirham as inheritance; they only.
left knowledge as inheritance; whoever takes it has taken an abundant share." Narrated by al-Tirmidhī.

safi-cedvel:12-13.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها الذين آمنوا) its i'rab has preceded, word by word and clause by clause [Note: In verse (9) of the sūra.]. (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (بين) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قدّموا). The reference in (ذلك) is to the advancing of charity. (لكم) attached to (خير). (الفاء) a conjunction. (لم) for negation only. (الفاء) causal (taʿlīliyya) — or connecting.
The clause «ناجيتم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قدّموا ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «ذلك خير ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لم تجدوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the response to the vocative: the condition, its verb and its apodosis.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور ...» has no grammatical position, being a causal explanation (taʿlīl) for the omitted apodosis of إن, i.e. "If you do not find, there is no blame upon you, for Allah is Forgiving ...".
13- (الهمزة) for the interrogative of affirmation (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī). (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle. (بين) like the first. (الفاء) resumptive. (إذ) an adverb containing the meaning of condition [Note: It may be for the past, it may be for the future, or in the meaning of إن.], attached to the content of the apodosis. (لم) for negation, conversion (to the past) and the jussive [Note: Or for negation and the jussive only.]. (الواو) parenthetical — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (عليكم) attached to (تاب). (الفاء) connecting the apodosis. (الواو) a conjunction in the four places. (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive, the returning pronoun being omitted, and the clause is the ṣila.].
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقدّموا..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted (من), attached to (أشفقتم).
(The interpreted maṣdar (ما تعملون..) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar (predicate) (خبير).
[Translator's note: The opening parenthesis before "The interpreted maṣdar" is unmatched in the source.]
The clause «أشفقتم ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption within the scope of the response to the vocative.
The clause «تقدّموا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «لم تفعلوا ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تاب الله ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical between the condition and the apodosis [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of تفعلوا.].
The clause «أقيموا ...» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «آتوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أقيموا.
The clause «أطيعوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أقيموا.
The clause «الله خبير ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause أشفقتم [Note: Or resumptive within the scope of the response to the vocative.].
The clause «تعملون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).

* Rhetoric:
The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying, Exalted is He: بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْواكُمْ صَدَقَةً.
That is: give charity before it. The original construction is used of one who has two hands. The metaphor may also be implicit (makniyya), by likening the private counsel to a human being.

* Benefits:
- The charity of private counsel..
Ibn ʿAbbās said: People questioned the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did so much that it became burdensome to him, so Allah the Exalted wished to lighten things for His Prophet ﷺ and to hold them back from that, and He commanded them to give charity before privately consulting the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Mujāhid said: They were forbidden from private consultation until they gave charity, and no one consulted him privately except ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him; he gave a dīnār in charity and consulted him. Then the concession was revealed. ʿAlī used to say: "There is a verse in the Book of Allah that no one acted upon before me and no one will act upon after me: it is the verse of private consultation."

safi-cedvel:14-19.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of wonder (al-istifhām al-taʿajjubī). (إلى الذين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تر) in the meaning of "تنظر" (look). (تولّوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent). (عليهم) attached to (غضب). (ما) negative, operating as ليس operates. (منكم) attached to the khabar (predicate) of ما [Note: Or it is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) هم.]. (لا) redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation. (منهم) attached to what (منكم) is attached to, so it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to it. (على الكذب) attached to (يحلفون). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya)..
The clause «لم تر ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تولّوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «غضب الله ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of (قوما).
The clause «ما هم منكم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (تولّوا) [Note: It may be resumptive, and so have no grammatical position..].
The clause «يحلفون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause تولّوا..
The clause «هم يعلمون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
15- (لهم) attached to (أعدّ). (ما) a relative noun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil of the fully conjugated (mutaṣarrif) verb ساء, the returning pronoun being omitted..
The clause «أعدّ الله ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «إنّهم ساء ما كانوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
[Translator's note: So in the source; the clause إنّهم ساء ... is presumably meant as explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya) or resumptive, since it is not the ṣila of ما.]
The clause «ساء ما كانوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «كانوا يعملون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يعملون» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا.
16- (الفاء) a conjunction. (عن سبيل) attached to (صدّوا). (الفاء) a conjunction. (لهم) attached to an advanced khabar of the postponed mubtadaʾ (عذاب).
The clause «اتّخذوا ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
The clause «صدّوا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اتّخذوا.
The clause «لهم عذاب» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اتّخذوا, caused by what preceded.
17- (عنهم) attached to (تغني). (لا) redundant to emphasise the negation. (من الله) attached to (تغني), with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "from His punishment". (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, i.e. "any availing at all". (فيها) attached to (خالدون)..
The clause «لن تغني ... أموالهم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أولئك أصحاب النار..» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.
The clause «هم فيها خالدون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from أصحاب, its governing word being the demonstrative — or from النار.
18- (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (تغني) [Note: Or it is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember).]. (جميعا) a ḥāl, accusative, from the pronoun in (يبعثهم) [Note: Or a tawkīd maʿnawī (semantic emphasis) of the absent pronoun in (يبعثهم).]. (الفاء) a conjunction. (له) attached to (يحلفون). (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle. (لكم) attached to the second (يحلفون)..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يحلفون) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "an oath like their oath to you".
(الواو) circumstantial. (على شيء) attached to an omitted khabar of أنّ. (ألا) for drawing attention (tanbīh). (هم) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun as mubtadaʾ whose khabar is الكاذبون.. and the nominal clause is the khabar of إنّ.]..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم على شيء) is in the position of the accusative, filling the place of the two objects of يحسبون..
The clause «يبعثهم الله ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يحلفون له» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يبعثهم.
The clause «يحلفون لكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (ما).
The clause «يحسبون ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «إنّهم ... الكاذبون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
19- (عليهم) attached to (استحوذ). (الفاء) a conjunction. (ألا إنّ ... هم الخاسرون) like ألا إنّهم هم الكاذبون.
The clause «استحوذ عليهم الشيطان» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أنساهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause استحوذ.
The clause «أولئك حزب الشيطان ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إنّ حزب ... الخاسرون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(16) جنّة: a noun meaning "covering"; its pattern is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn, and its ʿayn and lām are from a single letter.

* Benefits:
- (كما)..
(كما) frequently occurs after clauses as an adjective in meaning, so it is a naʿt of a maṣdar or a ḥāl. Both are possible in His saying, Exalted is He, in the verse we are dealing with: فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ, and in His saying, Exalted is He: يَوْمَ نَطْوِي السَّماءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ لِلْكُتُبِ كَما بَدَأْنا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ نُعِيدُهُ وَعْداً عَلَيْنا إِنَّا كُنَّا فاعِلِينَ. If you take it as a naʿt of a maṣdar, it is governed either by نعيده, i.e. (نعيد أول خلق إعادة) (We shall repeat the first creation with a repetition), or by نطوي, i.e. "We shall do this mighty act like Our doing this act". If you take it as a ḥāl, the one it describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl) is the object of نعيده, i.e. "We shall repeat it resembling that which We began".
This ruling also applies to the word «كذلك».

safi-cedvel:20-20.t:
* I'rab:
(في الأذلّين) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أولئك)..
The clause «إنّ الذين يحادّون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يحادّون ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «أولئك في الأذلّين» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(الأذلّين) plural of الأذلّ, an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from the triliteral ذلّ; its pattern is أفعل, and it has come in the plural because it bears the definite article (أل).

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(اللام) the lām of the oath. (أنا) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the latent (mustatir) pronoun that is the fāʿil (agent) of أغلبنّ. (الواو) a conjunction. (رسلي) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the latent pronoun that is the agent of أغلبنّ, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «كتب الله ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أغلبنّ ...» has no grammatical position, being the response to the oath represented by the verb كتب ...
The clause «إنّ الله قويّ» has no grammatical position, being explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) negative. (بالله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يؤمنون). (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya). (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle. (أو) a conjunction in the three places. (في قلوبهم) attached to (كتب), by its being made to imply (taḍmīn) the meaning of "أثبت" (He established). (بروح) attached to (أيّدهم). (منه) attached to a naʿt (adjective) of روح. (الواو) a conjunction. (من تحتها) attached to (تجري) [Note: Or attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأنهار.], with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "from beneath its trees". (خالدين) a ḥāl from the absent pronoun in (يدخلهم) [Note: Or a ḥāl from جنّات.]. (عنهم) attached to (رضي), and (عنه) attached to (رضوا). (أولئك حزب ... هم المفلحون) the i'rab of its like has preceded [Note: In verse (19) of this sūra.]..
The clause «لا تجد ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يؤمنون بالله ...» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of (قوما).
The clause «يوادّون ...» is in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb تجد [Note: If it is in the meaning of تعلم (know).. Or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the object of تجد if it is in the meaning of تلقى (meet); it is also valid for it to be another naʿt of (قوما).].
The clause «حادّ ...» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «كانوا آباؤهم ...» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl.
[Translator's note: The source quotes the clause as «كانوا آباؤهم»; the Quranic text is كانُوا آباءَهُمْ.]
The clause «أولئك كتب ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كتب ...» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (أولئك).
The clause «أيّدهم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كتب.
The clause «يدخلهم ...» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause كتب.
The clause «تجري ... الأنهار» is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of جنّات.
The clause «رضي الله عنهم» is in the position of the nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك) [Note: Or it has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption.].
The clause «رضوا عنه» is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause رضي الله.
The clause «أولئك حزب ...» has no grammatical position, being a resumption confirming the content of what preceded.
The clause «إنّ حزب الله ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(روح) a noun meaning light, or guidance, or proof, or mercy, or victory, or Jibrīl, peace be upon him; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
The marvellous ordering (al-tartīb al-rāʾiʿ): in His saying, Exalted is He: وَلَوْ كانُوا آباءَهُمْ أَوْ أَبْناءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ.
He put the fathers first, because their sons are obliged to obey them and to keep company with them in this world in what is right; He put the sons second, because they are more closely attached to them, being their very livers; He put the brothers third, because they are their helpers:
أخاك أخاك إن من لا أخا له ... كساع إلى الهيجا بغير سلاح
(Your brother, your brother! For one who has no brother is like one running to battle without a weapon.)
And He ended with the kinsfolk, because reliance on them and mutual help through them generally comes after the brothers.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {قَدْ سَمِعَ}: «قد» here is for expectation (tawaqquʿ). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the woman who disputed were both expecting that Allah would hear her dispute and complaint and would send down in that something to relieve her. Clear pronunciation of the dāl before the sīn is the reading of the group, except Abū ʿAmr and the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī]. It is reported of al-Kisāʾī that he said: 'Whoever pronounces the dāl clearly before the sīn has a non-Arab tongue and is not an Arab.' This is not to be dwelt on. «في زَوْجِها» means: concerning his affair, namely his zihār (declaring her like his mother's back) against her."
His saying: {وتشتكي إِلَى الله}: two views are possible. The more apparent is that it is conjoined to «تُجادِلُك», so it too is a ṣila. The second: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e., she disputes with you complaining of her condition to Allah; likewise the clause of His saying {والله يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمآ}, though the circumstantial reading is more remote there.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {الذين يُظَاهِرُونَ}: the disagreement about «يُظاهِرون» was already given in Sūrat al-Aḥzāb, and likewise about «اللائي», which spares repeating it here. Ubayy read here «يَتَظاهَرُون», and from him also «يَتَظَهَّرُوْن». There are two views on «الذين». One: it is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is His saying {مَّا هُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ}. The second: it is accusative through «بصير» [in the previous verse], according to Sībawayh's view that faʿīl may operate; Makkī said it. He means that Sībawayh makes the faʿīl, one of the forms of intensiveness, operate; this is a view that has been criticized in Sībawayh's name, because he cited as evidence for its operating the poet's saying:
4238 - Until a weary, languid one, working at a tiring hour, drove her on ... she spent the night restless, and he spent the night unsleeping
and it was answered that «مَوْهِناً» is an adverb of time, and adverbs are operated upon by whiffs of verbs. This question has a place more fitting than here, but the meaning refuses what Makkī said.
The majority read «أمَّهاتِهم» in the accusative according to the pure Ḥijāzī dialect, as in {مَا هذا بَشَراً} [Yūsuf: 31]. ʿĀṣim in one transmission read it nominative according to the Tamīmī dialect, which is in fact the analogical rule since the particle is not specific [to nouns]. ʿAbd Allāh read «بأمَّهاتهم» with the redundant bāʾ, which allows both dialects. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The bāʾ is added in the dialect of those who put the accusative." I say: this is Abū ʿAlī's view; he holds that the bāʾ is added only when «ما» is operative, so it is not added in the Tamīmī nor in the Ḥijāzī if some obstacle prevents its operating, as in "mā in Zaydun bi-qāʾimin". This is refuted by the saying of al-Farazdaq, who is a Tamīmī:
4239 - By your life, Maʿn is not one to abandon his right ... nor is Maʿn a postponer, nor one who makes things easy
and by another's saying:
4240 - By your life, Abū Mālik is not ... weak, nor is his strength feeble
for he added it after «ما» followed by «إنْ».
His saying: {مُنكَراً مِّنَ القول وَزُوراً}: two adjectives of an omitted maṣdar, i.e., "an objectionable saying", and zūr, i.e., a lie and a slander; Makkī said so, and there is something to consider in it, for the implied form becomes: "they surely say an objectionable saying of speech", so that His saying «من القول» has no benefit. It is preferable to say: two adjectives of an omitted object understood from the meaning, i.e., "they say something objectionable of speech", so that the adjective gives something other than what the described noun gave.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {والذين يُظَاهِرُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ. His saying «فتحريرُ رقبةٍ» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, i.e., "so upon them [is]"; or an agent of an implied verb, i.e., "so there is required of them the freeing"; or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e., "so what is obligatory upon them is the freeing". On all three implied forms the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the fāʾ entered because the mubtadaʾ contains the sense of a condition.
His saying: {لِمَا قَالُواْ}: there are several views on this lām. First: it is attached to «يعودون». Under this are several meanings. One: those who by habit used to say this saying in the Jāhiliyya, then return to its like in Islam. Two: then they make good what they said, because one who makes good a matter returns to it, and of this is "a rain came back upon what it had spoiled", i.e., it repaired it by amending; the meaning is that making good this saying and remedying it, by his giving expiation, so that their condition returns to what it was before the zihār. Three: that «ما قالوا» means what they forbade themselves by the wording of zihār, treating the saying as the thing spoken about, like what is mentioned at His saying the Exalted {وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ} [Maryam: 80]; the meaning: then they want to return to physical contact. Al-Zamakhsharī said that. I say: this third is the meaning of what is transmitted from Mālik, al-Ḥasan and al-Zuhrī: "then they return to intercourse", i.e., they return to what they said they would not return to; so if he made zihār then had intercourse, expiation is incumbent on him according to these. Four: «لما قالوا» means: they say it a second time; so if he said "you are to me as my mother's back" once, there is no expiation, because he has not returned to what he said. This is transmitted from Bukayr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ashajj, Abū Ḥanīfa, Abū al-ʿĀliya and al-Farrāʾ among others, and is the view of the Ẓāhirī jurists. Five: the meaning is that he resolves to keep her and does not divorce her after the zihār, until a time passes in which he could have divorced her; this is the "return" to what he said, and it is the view of al-Shāfiʿī and Mālik, and of Abū Ḥanīfa also. He said: the return here is not repetition of the saying, but in the sense of resolve on intercourse.
Makkī said: "The lām is attached to «يعودون», i.e., they return to intercourse with the one about whom zihār was said, who are the wives; so «ما» and the verb are a maṣdar, i.e., 'to what they say', the maṣdar being in the position of an object, like 'this is a dirham, ḍarb al-amīr', i.e., what is struck by the ruler; so the meaning of 'to their saying' is 'to the one spoken about with zihār', i.e., 'to intercourse with her'." I say: this is the meaning of al-Zamakhsharī's saying in the third view, whose explanation preceded from al-Ḥasan, al-Zuhrī and Mālik, except that Makkī restricted it to «ما» being a maṣdar particle so that the interpreted maṣdar takes the place of a passive participle.
There is something to consider in it, as that is permitted even if «ما» is not a maṣdar particle, being in the sense of "that which" or an indefinite described noun. Indeed, making it not a maṣdar particle is preferable, because the interpreted maṣdar is secondary to the explicit maṣdar, the explicit being the origin of the interpreted one, and putting a maṣdar in the place of a passive participle is contrary to the origin; so departure from the origin would be required in two things: the interpreted maṣdar,
then its occurring in the position of a passive participle; and what is preserved from their speech is only putting the explicit maṣdar in place of the object, not the interpreted maṣdar; so know it. It should not be said that making it a non-maṣdar requires an implied omitted muḍāf to make the meaning sound, i.e., "they return to intercourse with the one from whom he made zihār", or "a woman from whom he made zihār", or "they return to keeping her", the origin being no omission; for this obligation is shared between us and you, since you too say that an implied muḍāf is necessary, i.e., "they return to intercourse with, or keeping of, the one about whom zihār was said". What indicates the permissibility of «ما» being non-maṣdar in this view is what Abū al-Baqāʾ pointed to, for he said: "It is attached to «يعودون», meaning 'they return to the one about whom it was said.' This is if you make «ما» a maṣdar particle, and you may make it mean 'that which' and an indefinite described noun."
The second: the lām is attached to «تحرير». There is fronting and postponing in the speech. The implied form: "Those who make zihār against their wives, upon them is the freeing of a slave for what they uttered of zihār, then they return to intercourse after that." This is what Makkī and others transmitted from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash. The Shaykh said: "It is nothing, because it spoils the structure of the verse." There is something to consider in it. We do not concede the spoiling of the structure when the meaning indicates the fronting and postponing; but we concede that claiming fronting and postponing is unnecessary, because it is contrary to the origin.
The third: the lām means «إلى». The fourth: it means «في». Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted these two, and they are very weak; even so, it is attached to «يَعُودون». The fifth: it is attached to «يقولون». Makkī said: "Qatāda said: then they return to what they said of prohibition and make it lawful; so on this the lām is attached to «يقولون»." I say: I do not know what Makkī said here, or how he understood its attachment to «يقولون» on Qatāda's interpretation; rather Qatāda's interpretation is explicit that it is attached to «يَعودون», and there is no basis for its attachment to «يقولون».

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {فَصِيَامُ} and «فإِطعامُ} are like His saying {فَتَحْرِيرُ} in the three views mentioned earlier. «مِنْ قبلِ» is attached to the preceding verb or "settling", i.e., "so there is required of him the freeing or fasting", or "upon him is such-and-such", before the two touch each other. The pronoun in «يتماسَّا» is for the one who made zihār and the one against whom it was made, as what precedes indicates them.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ}: several views. One: it is accusative through «عذابٌ مُهينٌ». Two: it is accusative through an implied verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied "they are humiliated" or "they are punished", or "that settles for them on the day He raises them". Al-Zamakhsharī implied «اذْكُرْ» (remember), saying: "to magnify the day". Three: it is accusative through «لهم», al-Zamakhsharī said, i.e., through the settling it contains, as it is a khabar. Four: it is accusative through «أَحْصاه»; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. There is unease in it, because the pronoun in «أحْصاه» returns to what they did.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {مَا يَكُونُ مِن نجوى}: «يكونُ» is complete (tāmma, needing no predicate) and «من نَجْوى» is its agent. «مِنْ» is redundant in it. «نجوى» is originally a maṣdar, so it may remain in its origin and be annexed to its agent, i.e., "there is not found any conspiring of three". It may also be with an omitted muḍāf, i.e., "of those having a secret conversation". It may also be applied to the persons conversing secretly, for emphasis. On these last two views «ثلاثة» is genitive in one of two ways: either a badal from the omitted «ذوي», or an adjective of it on the second implied form; or a badal or adjective of «نَجْوَى» on the third implied form.
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ثلاثةً» and «خمسةً» in the accusative as a ḥāl. There are two views on its owner. One: it is omitted together with its nominative operator, its implied form being "they converse as three", omitted because «نجوى» indicates it. The second: it is the latent pronoun in «نجوى» if we make it mean the ones conversing; al-Zamakhsharī said so. Makkī said: "In speech the nominative of «ثلاثة» is permitted as a badal from the position of «نَجْوى», because its position is nominative and «مِنْ» is redundant; and if you put «ثلاثة» in the accusative as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun, when you make «نجوى» mean the ones conversing, it is permitted in speech." I say: as for the nominative, as far as I know it was not read, though it is permitted outside the Quran as he said. As for the accusative, you have learned who read it, so it is as though he did not come across it.
His saying: {إِلاَّ هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ}, «إلاَّ هو خامسُهم», {إِلاَّ هُوَ مَعَهُمْ}: all these clauses after «إلاَّ» are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, i.e., none of these things is found except in one of these states; so the exception is an emptied exception (mufarragh) from the general states.
