Abū Jaʿfar read «ما تكونُ» with the feminine tāʾ because «النجوى» is feminine. Abū al-Faḍl said: but the masculine is more common in this chapter, as in the majority's reading, because it is predicated of «مِن نجوى», which is a masculine generic noun.
His saying: {وَلاَ أَكْثَرَ}: the majority read it genitive, conjoined to the wording of «نجوى». Al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Abū Ḥaywa and Yaʿqūb read «ولا أكثرُ» nominative. There are two views: one, it is conjoined to the position of «نَجْوى», because it is nominative, with «مِنْ» redundant in it. If it is a maṣdar, it is with an omitted muḍāf as above, i.e., "of those having a secret conversation"; if it means the ones conversing, there is no need for that. The second: «أَدْنى» is a mubtadaʾ and {إِلاَّ هُوَ مَعَهُمْ} is its khabar, so «ولا أكثرُ» is conjoined to the mubtadaʾ, and then «ولا أَدْنَى» is of the type of conjunction of clauses, not of single words.
Al-Ḥasan and Yaʿqūb also, and Mujāhid and al-Khalīl, read «ولا أكبرُ» with the single-dotted bāʾ and nominative, as above. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُنْبِهِمْ», from anbaʾa, except that he omitted the hamza and put kasra on the hāʾ; and it has been read likewise but retaining the hamza and with ḍamma on the hāʾ. The majority read it doubled, from nabbaʾa.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {وَيَتَنَاجَوْنَ}: Ḥamza read «يَنْتَجُوْنَ», from intijāʾ, from najwā. The rest read «يتناجَوْن», from tanājī, also from najwā. Abū ʿAlī said: "The forms iftiʿāl and tafāʿul run the same course, and hence they kept the sound form in «izdawajū» and «iʿtawarū» when they were in the sense of «tazāwajū» and «taʿāwanū». And «حتى إِذَا اداركوا» and «ادركوا» [al-Aʿrāf: 38] have come." I say: the consensus on «تناجَيْتُمْ», «فلا تَتَناجوا» and «وتناجَوْا» supports the majority's reading, for these are from tafāʿul and nothing else, except what is transmitted from ʿAbd Allāh that he read «إذا انْتَجَيْتُم فلا تَنْتَجُوا». The Shaykh transmitted from the Kufans and al-Aʿmash «فلا تَنْتَجُوا» like ʿAbd Allāh's reading. The origin of «تَنْتَجُون» is «tantajiyūna» and of «يتناجَوْن» is «yatanājayūna»; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy and dropped, so two quiescent letters met and the yāʾ was dropped for their meeting. Or we say: the weak letter was vowelled and what precedes it was open, so it was turned into alif; two quiescent letters met, so the first was dropped and the fatḥa remained indicating the alif.
[And] Abū Ḥaywa read «بالعِدْوان» with kasra on the ʿayn.

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The two readings «ليحزنَ», with ḍamma and with fatḥa, were already discussed in Āl ʿImrān. It has also been read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the zāy, as predicated of the relative noun after it, which is then the agent.
And His saying: {وَلَيْسَ بِضَآرِّهِمْ}: the noun of «ليس» may be a pronoun returning to Satan, and it may return to the grief understood from «ليحزنَ»; al-Zamakhsharī said it. The first is preferable because what it returns to is stated explicitly. [And] al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «ومعصيات» as a plural.
His saying: {لَوْلاَ يُعَذِّبُنَا} [al-Mujādila: 8]: this exhortative clause is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥafṣ and Abū Bakr, with disagreement from him, read «انشُزوا» with ḍamma on the shīn in both places; the rest read it with kasra. They are two dialects with one meaning. One says nashaza, i.e., rose, yanshizu and yanshuzu, like ʿarasha yaʿrishu and yaʿrushu, and ʿakafa yaʿkifu and yaʿkufu. This root has already been discussed in al-Baqara.
His saying: {فِي المجالس}: ʿĀṣim read «المجالس» as a plural, considering that each of them has a sitting place. The rest read the singular, since what is meant is the sitting place of the Messenger ﷺ, which is better than its being a singular intended as a plural. It has also been read «في المجلَس» with fatḥa on the lām, which is the maṣdar, i.e., make room in your sitting and do not crowd. Al-Ḥasan, Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, ʿĪsā and Qatāda read «تَفاسَحُوا». Al-fusḥa is spaciousness; fasaḥa lahu means he made room for him.
His saying: {والذين أُوتُواْ}: it may be conjoined to «الذين آمنوا», so it is a conjunction of the specific to the general, because those given knowledge are some of the believers among them. It may also be that «والذين أُوْتُوا» is a conjunction of attributes, i.e., the attributes belong to one entity, as if it were said: Allah raises the believers who are scholars. «دَرَجاتٍ» is a second object; its like was already discussed in al-Anʿām. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the speech is complete at His saying «منكم», and «الذين أُوْتُوا» is accusative through an implied verb, i.e., "and He singles out those given knowledge for degrees", or "and raises them in degrees". [Translator's note: the source reads «اللمَ» (a typographical error) where «العلمَ» (knowledge) is clearly meant; translated as "knowledge".]

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُواْ}: there are three views on this «إذْ». One: it is in its normal sense of the past. The meaning: you neglected that in the past, so make it up by establishing prayer; Abū al-Baqāʾ said it. Two: it means «إذا», as in His saying {إِذِ الأغلال} [Ghāfir: 71], which has already been discussed. Three: it means the conditional «إنْ», which is close to the previous, though the difference between «إنْ» and «إذا» is well known. It is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr «خَبِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ» with the yāʾ of the third person; the well-known [reading] from him is with the tāʾ of address like the group.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {مَّا هُم مِّنكُمْ وَلاَ مِنْهُمْ}: three views are possible on this clause. One: it is resumptive with no position in i'rab. He reports of them that they are not of the pure believers nor of the pure disbelievers, but rather as in His saying: {مُّذَبْذَبِينَ بَيْنَ ذلك لاَ إلى هؤلاء وَلاَ إِلَى هؤلاء} [al-Nisāʾ: 143]. So the pronoun in «ما هم» returns to those who turned away, who are the hypocrites, and in «منهم» it returns to the Jews, i.e., the pure disbelievers. The second: it is a ḥāl from the agent of «تَوَلَّوا», and the meaning is as before. The third: it is a second adjective of «قوماً», so on this the pronoun in «ما هم» returns to «قوماً», who are the Jews, and the pronoun in «منهم» returns to those who turned away, meaning: the Jews are not of you, O believers, nor of the hypocrites, and even so the hypocrites took them as allies; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it. But in it the pronouns clash, for the pronoun in «ويَحْلِفون» returns to those who turned away. On the first two views the pronouns are the same, returning to those who turned away; on the third they differ, as you have learned in its explanation.
His saying: {وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ}: a circumstantial clause, i.e., they know it is a lie, so their oath is a plunging oath (yamīn ghamūs) for which they have no excuse.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {أَيْمَانَهُمْ جُنَّةً}: two objects of «اتَّخذوا». The majority read «أَيْمانَهم» with fatḥa on the hamza, the plural of yamīn. Al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, as a maṣdar. And His saying {لَّن تُغْنِيَ عَنْهُمْ} was already treated in Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {استحوذ}: it came in its original form, which is eloquent in usage, though irregular by analogy. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, produced it by analogy and read «استحاذ», like istaqāma. This root was given in Sūrat al-Nisāʾ at His saying: {أَلَمْ نَسْتَحْوِذْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 141].

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {كَتَبَ الله لأَغْلِبَنَّ}: «كَتَبَ» may run the course of an oath, and so be answered with what an oath is answered with. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is also said that it is the answer of «كَتَبَ» because it means 'said'." This is nothing, because «قال» does not require an answer, so the correct view is what I gave first. It may also be that «لأَغْلِبَنَّ» is the answer of an implied oath, but that is not apparent.

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {يُوَآدُّونَ}: it is the second object of «تَجِدُ». It is also possible that [«تجد»] is the one taking a single object, meaning "meet, encounter", in which case «يوادُّون» is a ḥāl or an adjective of «قوماً». The wāw in «ولو كانوا» is circumstantial, and its explanation has been given more than once. He mentioned fathers first because obedience to them is obligatory on their sons, then the sons second because they are closest to the hearts and are their kernels:
4241 - For our children among us ... are our livers walking on the earth
The well-known verses in the Ḥamāsa. He made brothers third because they are the helpers, in the position of the upper arm to the forearm. He said:
4242 - Your brother, your brother! For he who has no brother ... is like one going to battle without arms
and the cousin of a man, know, is his wing ... and can the hawk rise without a wing?
Then he made the clan fourth, because by it one calls for help and on it one relies. He said:
4243 - They do not ask their brother, when he summons them ... in calamities, for what proof he has said
Abū Rajāʾ read «عشيراتِهم» in the plural, as Abū Bakr read it in al-Tawba likewise. The majority read «كَتَبَ» in the active voice, the agent being Allah the Exalted, with «الإِيمانَ» accusative; Abū Ḥaywa, and ʿĀṣim in the transmission of al-Mufaḍḍal, read «كُتِبَ» in the passive, with «الإِيمانُ» nominative through it. The pronoun in «منه» refers to Allah the Exalted. It is also said that it returns to faith, because it is a spirit by which the believers live in both abodes.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجَادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْتَكِي إِلَى اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَا إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ (١))
His saying (وَتَشْتَكِي): it may be conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «تُجَادِلُ», and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَأَشْفَقْتُمْ أَنْ تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْوَاكُمْ صَدَقَاتٍ فَإِذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا وَتَابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ (١٣))
His saying (فَإِذْ لَمْ): it is said: «إِذْ» is in the sense of إِذَا, as we mentioned on His saying (إِذِ الْأَغْلَالُ فِي أَعْنَاقِهِمْ).
It is also said: it is in the sense of the conditional إِنْ. It is also said: it keeps its proper sense, referring to the past, and the meaning is: "you neglected that in the past, so make up for it by establishing the prayer".

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطَانُ فَأَنْسَاهُمْ ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطَانِ أَلَا إِنَّ حِزْبَ الشَّيْطَانِ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ (١٩))
His saying (اسْتَحْوَذَ): the wāw was kept sound here only as a formation according to the original; its regular form would be اسْتَحَاذَ, like اسْتَقَامَ.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ يُظَاهِرُونَ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ مَا هُنَّ أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ إِنْ أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ إِلَّا اللَّائِي وَلَدْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّهُمْ لَيَقُولُونَ مُنْكَرًا مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَزُورًا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ (٢))
His saying (أُمَّهَاتِهِمْ): with kasra on the tāʾ, as the khabar (predicate) of «مَا»; and with ḍamma on it [أُمَّهَاتُهُمْ], according to the dialect of Tamīm.
And (مُنْكَرًا), i.e. "a reprehensible saying".

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ (٢١))
His saying (لَأَغْلِبَنَّ): it is the answer to an omitted oath.
It is also said: it is the answer to كَتَبَ, because it is in the sense of قَالَ (said).

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَا تَجِدُ قَوْمًا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ يُوَادُّونَ مَنْ حَادَّ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَوْ كَانُوا آبَاءَهُمْ أَوْ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ أَوْ إِخْوَانَهُمْ أَوْ عَشِيرَتَهُمْ أُولَئِكَ كَتَبَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَأَيَّدَهُمْ بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ وَيُدْخِلُهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ وَرَضُوا عَنْهُ أُولَئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ أَلَا إِنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ (٢٢))
His saying (يُوَادُّونَ): it is the second object of تَجِدُ, or a ḥāl (circumstantial), or an adjective (ṣifa) of قَوْمٍ.
On this [last view], «تَجِدُ» means "you come across". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يُظَاهِرُونَ مِنْ نِسَائِهِمْ ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا قَالُوا فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا ذَلِكُمْ تُوعَظُونَ بِهِ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ (٣))
His saying (وَالَّذِينَ يُظَاهِرُونَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ» is also a mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "then upon them [is the freeing of a slave]"; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the [first] mubtadaʾ. His saying «مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَتَمَاسَّا» is construed according to the meaning, i.e. "then upon each one".
His saying (لِمَا قَالُوا): the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to يَعُودُونَ, and the meaning is "they return to what was said about it", this if you make «مَا» maṣdariyya.
You may also take it in the sense of الَّذِي (that which), or as an indefinite noun with a description.
It is also said: the lām is in the sense of فِي; and it is also said: in the sense of إِلَى. It is also said: there is an anteposition in the sentence, its implied form being "then they return; so upon them is the freeing of a slave on account of what they said". The returning here does not mean repeating the act, but rather resolving upon intercourse.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا فَيُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا أَحْصَاهُ اللَّهُ وَنَسُوهُ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ (٦))
His saying (يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ), i.e. "they will be punished", or "they will be humiliated", or "that is established on the day He resurrects them". It is also said: it is an adverb (ẓarf) of «أَحْصَاهُ».

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ مَا يَكُونُ مِنْ نَجْوَى ثَلَاثَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ رَابِعُهُمْ وَلَا خَمْسَةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ سَادِسُهُمْ وَلَا أَدْنَى مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَا أَكْثَرَ إِلَّا هُوَ مَعَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كَانُوا ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُمْ بِمَا عَمِلُوا يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ (٧))
His saying (ثَلَاثَةٍ): it is genitive because «نَجْوَى» is annexed to it; and نَجْوَى is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of التَّنَاجِي or الِانْتِجَاء (confiding together).
It is also possible for النَّجْوَى to be a noun for those who confide together, so that «ثَلَاثَةٍ» would be an adjective (ṣifa) or a badal (substitute).
(وَلَا أَكْثَرَ) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the number. It is also read in the nominative [وَلَا أَكْثَرُ], as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what follows it as the khabar (predicate).
It may also be conjoined to the position of «مِنْ نَجْوَى».

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى الَّذِينَ نُهُوا عَنِ النَّجْوَى ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِمَا نُهُوا عَنْهُ وَيَتَنَاجَوْنَ بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَمَعْصِيَةِ الرَّسُولِ وَإِذَا جَاءُوكَ حَيَّوْكَ بِمَا لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ وَيَقُولُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَوْلَا يُعَذِّبُنَا اللَّهُ بِمَا نَقُولُ حَسْبُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَهَا فَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ (٨))
His saying (وَيَتَنَاجَوْنَ) is also read (وَيَنْتَجُونَ), and the two have the same meaning; one says تَنَاجَوْا and انْتَجَوْا.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Mujādala
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجادِلُكَ في زَوْجِها﴾ — assimilating (idghām) the dāl into the sīn is good, because the two points of articulation are close. It is read "قَد سَّمِعَ اللَّهُ", with the dāl assimilated into the sīn, so that the speaker does not pronounce a dāl. This is good only because sīn and dāl are among the letters of the tip of the tongue, so assimilating the dāl into the sīn strengthens the letter. Pronouncing the dāl distinctly (iẓhār) is also permissible, because the place of the dāl — even though it is close to the place of the sīn — is a separate zone. From the place of the dāl come ṭāʾ and tāʾ: these three letters have one place; while sīn, zāy and ṣād are from one place and are called the whistling letters (ḥurūf al-ṣafīr). For that reason pronouncing the dāl distinctly is permissible.
This verse was revealed on account of Khawla bint Thaʿlaba and Aws ibn al-Ṣāmit, who were of the Anṣār. He said to her: "You are to me like my mother's back"; and it has been said he said to her: "You are to me like my mother". This expression was among those by which the people of the Jāhiliyya used to divorce. They have transmitted «that she went to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Aws married me when I was young and sought after; then when my age had passed and my womb had scattered (nathara) — that is, my children had become many — he made me to him like his mother." It is transmitted that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: "I have nothing concerning your matter." So she complained to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and said: "O Allah, I complain to You." It is also transmitted that among the things she said to the Prophet, upon him be peace, was: "I have small children: if I leave them with him they will be lost, and if I keep them with me they will go hungry." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, sent down the expiation (kaffāra) for ẓihār.» In this there is evidence that what the Jāhiliyya used to divorce by is not a divorce unless Islam brings that, as with what they said of "خَلِيَّةٌ" (free), "بَرِيَّةٌ" (quit) and "حَبْلُكِ عَلى غارِبِكِ" (your rope is on your withers); and the origin of their saying "أنْتِ طالِقٌ" (you are divorced): when Islam brought a ruling on it, it proceeded according to the ruling of Islam.

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ مِنكم مِن نِسائِهِمْ ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾ — the meaning is: "those wives who are made like mothers are not mothers". ﴿إنْ أُمَّهاتُهم إلا اللائِي ولَدْنَهُمْ﴾: the meaning is: "their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, mentioned mothers in another place, saying: ﴿وَأُمَّهاتُكُمُ اللاتِي أرْضَعْنَكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 23]; so Allah made known that the women who suckle are mothers. The meaning is: "their mothers are none but those who gave birth to them", that is, those who bore them and those who suckled them; so the wives are not like these. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that this is reprehensible and false, and said: ﴿وَإنَّهم لَيَقُولُونَ مُنْكَرًا مِنَ القَوْلِ وزُورًا وإنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾: He pardoned them and forgave them by imposing the expiation upon them. "اَلَّذِينَ" is in the position of the nominative (fī mawḍiʿ rafʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject; ibtidāʾ), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾; "أُمَّهاتِهِمْ" is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as the khabar of "ما"; the meaning is: "لَيْسَ هُنَّ بِأُمَّهاتِهِمْ" (they are not their mothers).

zajjaj:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ يُظاهِرُونَ﴾ (the verse) — "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject; ibtidāʾ), and its khabar (predicate) is "فَعَلَيْهِمْ تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ" (then upon them is the freeing of a slave); "عَلَيْهِمْ" was not mentioned because there is evidence for it in the speech. If you wish, you may imply "فَكَفّارَتُهم تَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ" (then their expiation is the freeing of a slave). ﴿مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَتَماسّا﴾: the people of knowledge differed. Some of them said: "the expiation is for the touching"; and some of them said: if he wants to return to her and remain (with her), whether he touches her or not, he makes expiation.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكم تُوعَظُونَ بِهِ﴾ — the meaning is: "that severity in the expiation is what you are admonished by". Some people said: the expiation is not obligatory until he says a second time: "You are to me like my mother's back". This is the saying of one who does not know the language, and it contradicts the saying of all the people of knowledge. Rather, the meaning is: "then they return with the return that is on account of the saying, and for that return the expiation becomes binding", not for every return. There is another view on it, that of al-Akhfash, which is that "لِما قالُوا" be made part of the ṣila of "فَتَحْرِيرُ رَقَبَةٍ" [Translator's note: i.e. attached to it]; so the meaning according to him is: "and those who pronounce ẓihār on their wives then return — then the freeing of a slave, for what they said". This is also a good position. The evidence against this speaker's claim that "ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما قالُوا" means that he says a second time "You are to me like my mother's back" is the saying of all the people of knowledge, and his own following of them on: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ يُؤْلُونَ مِن نِسائِهِمْ تَرَبُّصُ أرْبَعَةِ أشْهُرٍ فَإنْ فاءُوا﴾ [al-Baqara: 226]: they agree that ﴿فَإنْ فاءُوا﴾ [al-Baqara: 226] does not mean "if they swear a second time"; and the meaning of "فاؤُوا" and "عادُوا" in the language is one and the same.
His saying: ﴿مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَتَماسّا﴾ — an allusion (kināya) to intercourse. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿وَإنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾ [al-Baqara: 237], where the meaning is: "before you consummate the marriage with them".

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَن لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيامُ شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتابِعَيْنِ﴾ — the meaning is: "whoever does not find the slave, his expiation is the fasting of two consecutive months"; or if you wish: "then upon him is the fasting of two consecutive months". Were it read "فَصِيامٌ شَهْرَيْنِ" (with tanwīn), it would be permissible, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أوْ إطْعامٌ في يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ﴾ [al-Balad: 14] ﴿يَتِيمًا ذا مَقْرَبَةٍ﴾ [al-Balad: 15]; but I know of no one who read it with tanwīn.
His saying: ﴿فَمَن لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ فَإطْعامُ سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا﴾ — "مَن" is in the position of the nominative, on the meaning: "whoever is unable to fast, his expiation is feeding sixty poor people"; and likewise "فَإطْعامٌ" with tanwīn (would be permissible), but I know of no one who read it so.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾ — "ذَلِكَ" is in the position of the nominative; the meaning is: "the obligation is that which We have described". The meaning of "لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ" is: so that you affirm what the Messenger of Allah brought, and affirm that Allah commanded us with it. ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: what We have described concerning ẓihār and the expiation are the limits of Allah. ﴿وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾, that is: for whoever does not affirm them; and "ألِيمٌ" means painful.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحادُّونَ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ كُبِتُوا كَما كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ — the meaning of "كُبِتُوا" is: they were abased and disgraced by punishment and by being overcome, as befell those before them who opposed Allah. The meaning of ﴿يُحادُّونَ اللَّهَ﴾ and "يُشاقُّونَ اللَّهَ" is: they are on a different side (ḥadd) from the one on which the friends of Allah are; and likewise "يُشّاقُونَ": they are on the side (shiqq) on which the enemies of Allah are.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا﴾ — "يَوْمَ" is accusative (manṣūb) by the sense of His saying: "وَلِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابٌ مُّهِينٌ يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا", that is: He will raise them gathered together in one state. ﴿فَيُنَبِّئُهم بِما عَمِلُوا﴾, that is: He informs them of that, so that they know the proof is binding against them.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ﴾ — that is: He knows everything in the heavens and everything in the earth, of what is manifest to the servants and of what is hidden.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ما يَكُونُ مِن نَجْوى ثَلاثَةٍ إلا هو رابِعُهُمْ﴾ — that is: there is no private gathering of three who keep something secret and confer about it privately but He is their fourth, knowing it; and He is in every place, that is, by knowledge. "نَجْوى" is derived from "اَلنَّجْوَةِ", which is what is raised up and set apart. You say: "فُلانٌ مِن هَذا المَكانِ بِنَجْوَةٍ" when he is at a distance from it. So the meaning of "يَتَناجَوْنَ" is: they withdraw together privately with what they want. Allah mentioned this verse because the hypocrites and the Jews used to confer privately, making the Muslims imagine that they were conferring about something that would harm and hurt them, so they grieved at that. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, forbade that private conference, but the hypocrites and the Jews returned to it; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, informed the Prophet ﷺ that they had returned to exactly that kind of private conference, and said: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ نُهُوا عَنِ النَّجْوى ثُمَّ يَعُودُونَ لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ ويَتَناجَوْنَ بِالإثْمِ والعُدْوانِ ومَعْصِيَتِ الرَّسُولِ﴾ [al-Mujādala: 8], that is: they enjoin one another to disobey the Messenger; ﴿وَإذا جاءُوكَ حَيَّوْكَ بِما لَمْ يُحَيِّكَ بِهِ اللَّهُ ويَقُولُونَ في أنْفُسِهِمْ لَوْلا يُعَذِّبُنا اللَّهُ بِما نَقُولُ﴾ [al-Mujādala: 8], that is: why does Allah not punish us for what we say? When they came to the Prophet ﷺ they would say: "al-sām ʿalaykum", and "اَلسّامُ" is death. Then they said: why does punishment not descend on us when we say this to the Prophet, upon him be peace? But Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, had promised them the punishment of the Hereafter, and disgrace in this world, and the manifest victory of Islam and of the cause of the Prophet ﷺ, and the triumph of his party. So He said: ﴿حَسْبُهم جَهَنَّمُ يَصْلَوْنَها﴾ [al-Mujādala: 8], and He said: ﴿كُبِتُوا كَما كُبِتَ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ [al-Mujādala: 5], and He said: ﴿فَإنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ الغالِبُونَ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 56]. And He fulfilled His promise, helped His army, made His religion prevail and abased His enemy.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا تَناجَيْتُمْ فَلا تَتَناجَوْا بِالإثْمِ والعُدْوانِ ومَعْصِيَتِ الرَّسُولِ وتَناجَوْا بِالبِرِّ والتَّقْوى﴾ — that is: when you withdraw together for a secret, do so only for righteousness and piety, and do not be like the Jews and the hypocrites. In "تَتَناجَوْا" there are three options: "فَلا تَتَناجَوْا", with two distinct tāʾs; and with one assimilated, doubled tāʾ: "فَلا تَناجَوْا" [Translator's note: presumably to be read with a doubled tāʾ, تَّناجَوْا, since it is described as assimilated]. The two tāʾs are assimilated only because they are two letters from one point of articulation, both voweled, and preceded by an alif, and assimilation can come after an alif, as in "دابَّةٌ" and "رادٌ". Distinct pronunciation (iẓhār) is permissible [Translator's note: the text has the misprint يَجُورُ for يَجُوزُ] because the two tāʾs are at the beginning of the word, and "لا" is a word standing on its own while "تَتَناجَوْا" is another word, so this structure is not fixed; for that reason distinct pronunciation is better, though assimilation is permissible. It is also permissible to drop a tāʾ because of the two tāʾs coming together: it is related from the Arabs: "تَبَيَّنُ هَذِهِ الخَصْلَةُ" and "تَتَبَيَّنُ هَذِهِ الخَصْلَةُ" (this trait becomes clear); and in the Quran: "لَعَلَّكم تَذَكَّرُونَ", "تَتَذَكَّرُونَ" and "تَذْكُرُونَ" are one. But I know of no one who read "وَلا تَناجَوْا" with one tāʾ; rather it is read "فَلا تَنْتَجُوا", that is, "لا تَفْتَعِلُوا" (the iftiʿāl form) from "اَلنَّجْوى".

zajjaj:10-10.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّما النَّجْوى مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ لِيَحْزُنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ — that is: private conference in sin and transgression is from Satan, so that he may grieve those who believe. "لِيُحْزِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا", with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy, is also permissible: the Arabs say "حَزَنَنِي الأمْرُ" and "أحْزَنَنِي" (the matter grieved me). ﴿وَلَيْسَ بِضارِّهِمْ شَيْئًا﴾, that is: the private conferring does not harm the believers at all; and it may be: "وَلَيْسَ بِضارِّهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ شَيْئًا" (and Satan does not harm them at all).
His saying: ﴿إلا بِإذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: nothing harms them except what Allah wills. ﴿وَعَلى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ المُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, that is: "they entrust their affair to Allah and seek refuge with Him from the accursed Satan."

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا قِيلَ لَكم تَفَسَّحُوا في المَجالِسِ﴾ — it is also read "فِي المَجْلِسِ", and it is read "تَفاسَحُوا". It has come in the exegesis that by the majlis here is meant the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ; and it has been said of the majālis: the positions of war, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿مَقاعِدَ لِلْقِتالِ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 121]. As for what they were commanded in the assembly of the Prophet, upon him be peace, it has been said that the verse was revealed on account of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shammās [Translator's note: so in the text; the reports usually name Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās], who was one of the people of the Ṣuffa; and those of wealth and rank who sat in the assembly of the Prophet ﷺ would, as it were, not make room for those beneath them. So Allah commanded the believers to be humble and to make room in the assembly for whoever wanted (to come to) the Prophet ﷺ, so that people might be equal in taking their share from him. ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فانْشُزُوا﴾, that is: when it is said "rise up" — "stand up" — then rise. This is as He said: ﴿وَلا مُسْتَأْنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍ إنَّ ذَلِكم كانَ يُؤْذِي النَّبِيَّ فَيَسْتَحْيِي مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 53]. It has also been said: ﴿وَإذا قِيلَ انْشُزُوا فانْشُزُوا﴾, that is: when it is said "stand up for a prayer, or for fulfilling a right, or for a testimony", then rise. "اُنْشُرُوا فانْشُرُوا" is also permissible; both are read, and both are transmitted from the Arabs: "نَشَرَ، يَنْشُرُ، ويَنْشِزُ" [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably نَشَزَ، يَنْشُزُ ويَنْشِزُ, i.e. the imperfect with ḍamma or kasra, corresponding to the two readings اُنْشُزُوا / اِنْشِزُوا].
His saying: ﴿يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنكم والَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ دَرَجاتٍ﴾ — the evidence for the superiority of the people of knowledge is what is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: «"The worship of the scholar for a single day equals the worship of the ignorant worshipper for forty years."»

zajjaj:12-12.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إذا ناجَيْتُمُ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْواكم صَدَقَةً﴾ — that is: when you meet the Messenger privately for a secret, offer charity before that, and do so. It has been said that the reason for that was that the rich used to seek private audience with the Prophet ﷺ and confide to him what they wanted, while the poor could not get access to the Prophet ﷺ as they did; so He imposed charity upon them before the private conference, so that they would refrain from that. It is transmitted that ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, wanted to confer privately with the Prophet ﷺ, so he gave in charity a dinar which he had sold for ten dirhams, before conferring with him. Then the zakāt abrogated that, and He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أأشْفَقْتُمْ أنْ تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ نَجْواكم صَدَقاتٍ فَإذْ لَمْ تَفْعَلُوا وتابَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكم فَأقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وآتُوا الزَّكاةَ وأطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ﴾ [al-Mujādala: 13], that is: obey Him in every command; and making room in the assembly is included in that, so that people might be close together in drawing near to the Prophet, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا قَوْمًا غَضِبَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ ما هم مِنكم ولا مِنهم ويَحْلِفُونَ عَلى الكَذِبِ وهم يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — these are the hypocrites, who took the Jews as allies. As for the meaning of His saying ﴿وَيَحْلِفُونَ عَلى الكَذِبِ﴾, its interpretation is indicated by His saying: ﴿وَيَحْلِفُونَ بِاللَّهِ إنَّهم لَمِنكم وما هم مِنكم ولَكِنَّهم قَوْمٌ يَفْرَقُونَ﴾ [al-Tawba: 56].
His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ﴾ [al-Mujādala: 18] — this is indicated by His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهم إلا أنْ قالُوا واللَّهِ رَبِّنا ما كُنّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 23] ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَذَبُوا عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 24].

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿اسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ فَأنْساهم ذِكْرَ اللَّهِ﴾ — the meaning of "اِسْتَحْوَذَ" in the language is: he gained mastery. One says "حُذْتُ الإبِلَ" and "حُزْتُها" when you have gained mastery over the camels and gathered them. This is among the forms that come out on their original pattern (without vowel-weakening); its like in speech is "أجْوَدْتُ" and "أطْيَبْتُ", while the more common is "أجَدْتُ" and "أطَبْتُ". However, "اِسْتَحْوَذَ" came on the original pattern because it was not said on the basis of "حاذَ"; for it was built on "اِسْتَفْعَلَ" from the very first, just as "اِفْتَقَرَ" was built on "اِفْتَعَلَ" — it is from "اَلْفَقْرُ" (poverty), yet "فَقُرَ" is not said from it, nor was it used without augmentation. And "حاذَ عَلَيْهِمُ الشَّيْطانُ" was not said. Had "اِسْتَحاذَ" come, it would have been correct, but "اِسْتَحْوَذَ" here is better, because the verb in this sense has only been used with augmentation.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أُولَئِكَ حِزْبُ الشَّيْطانِ﴾ — Abū ʿUbayda said: the ḥizb of Satan is the army of Satan. The origin in the language is that ḥizb is a gathering and a group; from it one says "قَدْ تَحَزَّبَ القَوْمُ" when the people have become factions, a group of this sort and a group of that sort.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُحادُّونَ اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ أُولَئِكَ في الأذَلِّينَ﴾ — we have already explained "يُحادُّونَ": its meaning is "يُشاقُّونَ", that is, they come to be on a side (ḥadd) other than that of the friends of Allah, and in a camp (shiqq) other than theirs. ﴿أُولَئِكَ في الأذَلِّينَ﴾, that is: those are among the overcome.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لأغْلِبَنَّ أنا ورُسُلِي﴾ — that is: Allah has decreed a firm decree. The prevailing of the messengers is of two kinds: whoever was sent with war prevails in war, and whoever of them was sent without war prevails by proof. ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾, that is: He protects His party from being abased, because He said, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿أُولَئِكَ في الأذَلِّينَ﴾ [al-Mujādala: 20]. Al-ʿAzīz is the one who is not overcome or subdued.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿لا تَجِدُ قَوْمًا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ﴾ to the end of the account — it has come in the exegesis that this verse was revealed on account of Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa. The Prophet ﷺ had resolved to march on the people of Mecca, and Ḥāṭib wrote explaining the matter to them and warning them so that they could take precautions. Then the revelation came down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When Ḥāṭib was rebuked for that, he mentioned that he had family in Mecca and had no one to shelter them, and that he had done it only so that his family would be protected. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the belief of the believer is corrupted by affection for the disbelievers through aiding them against the believers; and Allah the Exalted made known that whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day does not take as an ally one who disbelieves, even if he were his father, or his mother, or his brother, or one of his kin.
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿أُولَئِكَ كَتَبَ في قُلُوبِهِمُ الإيمانَ﴾ — He means those who do not show affection to whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, and who ally themselves with the believers.
His saying: ﴿وَأيَّدَهم بِرُوحٍ مِنهُ﴾, that is: He strengthened them with the light of faith, by giving life to faith. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ أوْحَيْنا إلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِن أمْرِنا ما كُنْتَ تَدْرِي ما الكِتابُ ولا الإيمانُ ولَكِنْ جَعَلْناهُ نُورًا نَهْدِي بِهِ مَن نَشاءُ مِن عِبادِنا﴾ [al-Shūrā: 52]; so likewise ﴿وَأيَّدَهم بِرُوحٍ مِنهُ﴾. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that this brings them to Paradise, and said: ﴿وَيُدْخِلُهم جَنّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِها الأنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهم ورَضُوا عَنْهُ أُولَئِكَ حِزْبُ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: those who do not show affection to whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, and who are of the believers; and the party of Allah, that is: those who enter into the gathering which Allah has chosen and been pleased with.
His saying: ﴿ألا إنَّ حِزْبَ اللَّهِ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ﴾ — "ألا" is a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh) and of emphasis (tawkīd) for the account; and ﴿المُفْلِحُونَ﴾ are those who attain abiding in perpetual bliss.
